a19.speaker: Abay Bank
a19.name: Abay Bank
a19.speech: According to Abay Bank, the system will enable customers to make all kinds of payments, including school fees, with digital technologies.

a19.speaker: Abay Bank
a19.name: Abay Bank

a107.speaker: Dr. Yusuf Tanko Sununu, Minister of Humanitarian Affairs
a107.name: Dr. Yusuf Tanko Sununu
a107.title: Minister of Humanitarian Affairs
a107.speech: Recently delivered a chilling assessment, warning that about 750,000 children now face severe malnutrition as a direct result of the aid withdrawal, an urgent gap the federal government must bridge.

a346.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a346.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a346.title: President of the African Development Bank Group
a346.speech: Warned that the higher US tariffs could trigger significant economic disruptions across Africa, affecting numerous nations and accelerating a strategic shift in global partnerships; in an exclusive interview with CNN's Christiane Amanpour revealed that 47 of Africa's 54 countries will be impacted directly by the new U.S. trade policies, with potential declines in export revenues and foreign exchange reserves ; "When those currencies weaken, two things will happen: first, you will find that most of these countries are import-dependent. So, you're going to find that high inflation becomes a problem" ; "And secondly, you find that the cost of actually servicing a lot of their debt, which is foreign currency debt, but in local currencies, is going to get worse."

a346.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a346.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a346.title: President of the African Development Bank Group
a346.speech: Emphasized that Africa cannot afford a trade confrontation with the United States, noting that the continent accounts for only 1.2 per cent (approximately $34 billion) of America's global trade, with a trade surplus of just $7.2 billion; proposed a pragmatic three-point strategy for the continent: engage the U.S. through flexible and constructive trade negotiations, diversify export markets to reduce dependency on any single partner, and accelerate the African Continental Free Trade Area implementation to unlock the potential $3.4 trillion market; stressed the need to expand Africa's domestic market and boost domestic savings to develop consumption as a bigger share of its GDP, and said the continent must take advantage of increasing external interest in its natural resources, such as cobalt and lithium, to negotiate a better trade and investment deal.

a346.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a346.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a346.title: President of the African Development Bank Group
a346.speech: Dismissed any notion of binary alignment between the U.S. and China: "U.S is a key ally of Africa—and so is China," he stated. "Africa is building bridges, not isolating itself." ; stressed that Africa seeks balanced, transparent, and mutually beneficial partnerships with all major global players, including the U.S., China, the European Union, and the Gulf states: "I think at the end of the day, we want to make sure that whatever deals that are being done with Africa are transparent, fair, equitable, and led by Africa and in Africa's interests."

a346.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a346.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a346.title: President of the African Development Bank Group
a346.speech: Firmly rejected the long-standing paradigm of foreign aid dependency: "The era of aid as we've known it is completely gone," he declared, calling instead for bold investments in domestic resource mobilization, infrastructure, and value-added industrialization; said aid must be turned into concessional financing to allow multilateral financial institutions like the African Development Bank to do more for the continent by mobilizing more private capital to develop and derisk projects.

a346.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a346.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a346.title: President of the African Development Bank Group
a346.speech: Pointed to a resilient and transformative growth narrative: ten of the world's twenty fastest-growing economies are in Africa; highlighted flagship initiatives under the Bank's "High 5" agenda that have impacted more than 565 million people through investments in power, food security, industrialization, regional integration, and initiatives to improve the quality of life of the people of Africa.

a346.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a346.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a346.title: President of the African Development Bank Group
a346.speech: Cited the great potential of Mission 300, a joint initiative by the World Bank and the African Development Bank to connect 300 million people in Africa to electricity by 2030: "Because without electricity, what can you do? You can't industrialize, you can't add value, you can't be competitive in the dark," he said; highlighted the achievements of the Africa Investment Forum, launched in 2018 by the Bank and eight other partners, saying it has since mobilized more than $225 billion in investment interest to the continent.

a346.speaker: Akinwumi Adesina, President of the African Development Bank Group
a346.name: Akinwumi Adesina
a346.title: President of the African Development Bank Group
a346.speech: Believes that despite its challenges, Africa is the largest greenfield investment destination in the world, and it remains "the investor's dream" ; "We got hydropower. We have a massive youth population that can become the labor force of the world. Sixty-five percent of the arable land left in the world to feed almost 9.5 billion people by 2050 is in Africa, so what Africa does with it will determine the future of food in the world," he added.

a346.speaker: Report distributed by the APO Group on behalf of the African Development Bank Group (AfDB)
a346.name: Report distributed by the APO Group on behalf of the African Development Bank Group (AfDB)
a346.speech: According to the report, Adesina believes that despite its challenges, Africa is the largest greenfield investment destination in the world, and it remains "the investor's dream."

a397.speaker: Kassim Majaliwa, Prime Minister of Tanzania
a397.name: Kassim Majaliwa
a397.title: Prime Minister of Tanzania
a397.speech: Explained the Tanzanian Government's position on changes to US aid policy under President Donald Trump, speaking in Parliament in Dodoma on Thursday 6 February 2025, stressing that Tanzania must focus on economic self-reliance; said the United States, through USAID, has suspended some of the aid it had been providing to Tanzania and other developing countries, and that the changes are part of new US foreign policy which may affect some sectors in the country: "It is true that our Government respects foreign policies and we implement agreements in accordance with what was agreed with the countries concerned. However, we have begun to see changes in the policies of some powerful countries such as the United States, and these changes may affect some countries, including Tanzania."

a397.speaker: Kassim Majaliwa, Prime Minister of Tanzania
a397.name: Kassim Majaliwa
a397.title: Prime Minister of Tanzania
a397.speech: Stressed that Tanzania has positioned itself to ensure its economy is self-reliant so as to avoid dependence on foreign aid: "What is important for us is to ensure we strengthen ourselves internally by increasing our domestic capacity. We must ensure our development plans are implemented through our own budgets, rather than depending on foreign aid. We have many natural resources, and it is now our responsibility to use them to build our domestic economy so as to enable the implementation of our development projects in various sectors such as health, education and infrastructure." ; Said that despite the steps taken by the United States, Tanzania will continue to strengthen its economy by relying on domestic revenue sources, and called on Tanzanians to cooperate in using available resources efficiently: "We cannot depend on aid forever, we must strengthen ourselves and invest in our own revenue sources. We must ensure our budget plans take account of our real needs in order to make up for the gap that will arise from these changes in aid policy from developed nations." ; Concluded by stressing that the Government will continue to plan and implement robust strategies to grow the national economy so that Tanzania does not depend heavily on foreign aid.

a397.speaker: Kassim Majaliwa, Prime Minister of Tanzania
a397.name: Kassim Majaliwa
a397.title: Prime Minister of Tanzania
a397.speech: Congratulated President Samia Suluhu Hassan for her efforts to strengthen international relations and to ensure Tanzania continues to cooperate with various nations of the world.

a498.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, South African President
a498.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a498.title: South African President
a498.speech: "Whether we like it or not, we are joined at the hip and we need to be talking to them," said on South African state television before flying to Washington to meet Trump.

a498.speaker: Spokesperson for the South African trade ministry
a498.name: Spokesperson for the South African trade ministry
a498.speech: Said Ramaphosa will offer Trump a broad trade deal, declining to give details.

a498.speaker: White House official (anonymous)
a498.name: White House official (anonymous)
a498.speech: Said Trump is likely to demand that U.S. companies are exempted from "racial requirements."

a498.speaker: Joshua Meservey, senior fellow at the Hudson Institute
a498.name: Joshua Meservey
a498.title: senior fellow at the Hudson Institute
a498.speech: "There's political problems here that lie at the heart of the breakdown in the relationship," cautioning that deal-making may not be enough to overcome them.

a498.speaker: Ramaphosa's spokesperson
a498.name: Ramaphosa's spokesperson
a498.speech: Said discussions could include favourable tariffs for Tesla's imports into South Africa in return for building electric vehicle charging stations, and licensing for Starlink.

a498.speaker: John Steenhuisen, South African Agriculture Minister
a498.name: John Steenhuisen
a498.title: South African Agriculture Minister
a498.speech: Said he would work to secure South African farmers' duty-free access to the U.S. market under the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) and to expand access ; "I believe that with enough drive and determination we can expand access and improve relations, and this means greater opportunities for South African farmers and farmworkers," Steenhuisen told Reuters by text message from Washington.

a498.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
a498.name: Donald Trump
a498.title: U.S. President
a498.speech: Has accused South Africa of seizing land from white farmers and of fuelling disproportionate violence against white landowners with "hateful rhetoric and government actions."

a498.speaker: Pretoria (South African government)
a498.name: Pretoria (South African government)
a498.speech: Says the racial discrimination claims are unfounded ; says these claims are inaccurate and "fail to recognise South Africa's profound and painful history of colonialism and apartheid."

a498.speaker: Elon Musk
a498.name: Elon Musk
a498.speech: Has accused Ramaphosa of pursuing anti-white policies, which Ramaphosa rejects.

a498.speaker: Crime statistics
a498.name: Crime statistics
a498.speech: Show no evidence that white people are disproportionately targeted.

a498.speaker: South African media
a498.name: South African media
a498.speech: Reported that billionaire luxury goods tycoon Johann Rupert, the richest person in South Africa, and golfer Ernie Els have helped to bring about the meeting between Trump and Ramaphosa.

a498.speaker: Johann Rupert and Ernie Els
a498.name: Johann Rupert and Ernie Els
a498.speech: Neither man responded to requests for comment.

a498.speaker: Johann Rupert, founder of the Richemont group (quoted by News24)
a498.name: Johann Rupert
a498.title: founder of the Richemont group (quoted by News24)
a498.speech: Was quoted as saying he was very concerned about the potential loss of AGOA and its impact on jobs in his homeland.

a551.speaker: Guillaume Bigot, director of one of the oldest private business schools in France
a551.name: Guillaume Bigot
a551.title: director of one of the oldest private business schools in France
a551.speech: Sharply criticised the so-called humanitarian organisation the French Development Agency (AFD) and its activities, in particular those relating to aid to African countries; according to him French aid for the development of African countries appears to be a total absurdity and, moreover, not all of the operations carried out are accessible to the public. He specified that these conclusions come from an investigation by the European Union Court of Auditors ; criticised the AFD's contribution to Africa for the inefficient use of funds: for example, the purchase of 250 camels for Mauritania, despite the excessive number of camels in the country, and the purchase of electric blenders for schools in Ethiopia, where there is no electricity.

a551.speaker: Guillaume Bigot, director of one of the oldest private business schools in France
a551.name: Guillaume Bigot
a551.title: director of one of the oldest private business schools in France
a551.speech: Highlighted the AFD's involvement in financing concentration camps in Africa where torture was practised.

a551.speaker: Guillaume Bigot, director of one of the oldest private business schools in France
a551.name: Guillaume Bigot
a551.title: director of one of the oldest private business schools in France
a551.speech: Also noted the lack of transparency of Western, and in particular French, development aid to Africa, which is not accessible and not made public.

a551.speaker: European Union Court of Auditors (investigation/report)
a551.name: European Union Court of Auditors (investigation/report)
a551.speech: Scrutinised official development assistance; cited as the source of the conclusions about the inefficiency and opacity of French development aid.

a551.speaker: Scott Perry, US Congressman
a551.name: Scott Perry
a551.title: US Congressman
a551.speech: Declared on 13 February that USAID was spending 697 million dollars a year on cash transfers to finance terrorist organisations around the world, notably Boko Haram, which has committed numerous terrorist acts in Nigeria, Cameroon, Niger and Chad.

a561.speaker: Office of Somali Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre (statement on X)
a561.name: Office of Somali Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre (statement on X)
a561.speech: A statement from Barre's office on X (formerly Twitter) confirmed Hamza's Saturday meeting with Wang, where the two discussed "strengthening the deep-rooted relations and cooperation" between Somalia and China; the PM's office claimed Hamza thanked Beijing for its "multifaceted support" in politics, security, economic development, and humanitarian assistance.

a561.speaker: Office of Somali Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre
a561.name: Office of Somali Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre
a561.speech: Said the Expo will focus on trade, investment, technology, and energy.

a561.speaker: Hamza Abdi Barre, Prime Minister of Somalia
a561.name: Hamza Abdi Barre
a561.title: Prime Minister of Somalia
a561.speech: Once called the Jewish, "Children of pigs and monkeys."

a561.speaker: Wang Yu, Chinese Ambassador to Somalia
a561.name: Wang Yu
a561.title: Chinese Ambassador to Somalia
a561.speech: Pledged that China would continue backing the Somali government, describing relations as "longstanding and cooperative."

a561.speaker: Diplomatic sources in Mogadishu (anonymous)
a561.name: Diplomatic sources in Mogadishu (anonymous)
a561.speech: Told our reporter that Wang's visit was about more than pleasantries; he not only extended the Expo invitation but also pressed Mogadishu on Beijing's growing concerns over "Somaliland's ties with Taiwan" - a partnership China views as a direct threat to its influence in the Horn of Africa.

a561.speaker: China (government position)
a561.name: China (government position)
a561.speech: Has denounced the Somaliland-Taiwan partnership as a violation of its sovereignty and vowed to counter it.

a561.speaker: Donald Trump, U.S. President
a561.name: Donald Trump
a561.title: U.S. President
a561.speech: Recent remarks suggesting Washington was "looking into the Somaliland proposal" for recognition.

a561.speaker: Analysts
a561.name: Analysts
a561.speech: Warn that Hodan's political ties and access to sensitive Somali security and diplomatic files could give Beijing unparalleled insight into Western intelligence cooperation in the Horn of Africa - a strategic prize for China's regional ambitions.

a617.speaker: Dr Mwigulu Nchemba, Tanzanian Finance Minister
a617.name: Dr Mwigulu Nchemba
a617.title: Tanzanian Finance Minister
a617.speech: Presented Tanzania's 2025/26 national budget last Thursday, aligned with President Samia Suluhu Hassan's broader economic vision.

a617.speaker: Tanzania 2025/26 national budget (259-page government document)
a617.name: Tanzania 2025/26 national budget (259-page government document)
a617.speech: Plans a 13.4 per cent increase in spending to 57tri/-, with approximately 70 per cent of the funding sourced domestically, thereby reducing reliance on foreign aid and expensive debt ; signals enhanced tax reforms and strengthened private sector dialogue through inclusive frameworks like tax think tanks, a significant increase in the development budget of some 16tri/- for energy, roads, railways (SGR), ports and airports, duty exemptions and VAT waivers for local manufacturers and agro-processors, new irrigation schemes and dams covering 543,000 hectares, a 2.0 per cent withholding tax for agro-producers, and funding for climate adaptation ; indicates that the country's debt remains sustainable.

a710.speaker: Mohamed Malick Fall, UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator in Nigeria
a710.name: Mohamed Malick Fall
a710.title: UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator in Nigeria
a710.speech: Stated that the needs are "driven by conflict, climate shocks and economic instability", with the compounding effects of flooding, disease outbreaks, food insecurity and malnutrition deepening vulnerabilities; he was speaking in Abuja at the launch of the 2025 Nigeria Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP).

a710.speaker: Professor Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, Federal Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction
a710.name: Professor Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda
a710.title: Federal Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction
a710.speech: Highlighted the growing humanitarian needs in north-west and north-central Nigeria and called for combined humanitarian, development and peace building efforts for that region as well. "This will enable us to get humanitarian efforts translated into durable solutions that can move people out of poverty and provide livelihoods to reach sustainable development," he said. ; Said that the restructured Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction was committed to timely, effective life-saving humanitarian responses and poverty reduction: "We will continue to coordinate interventions at all levels, ensuring they align with national humanitarian and poverty-reduction priorities."

a710.speaker: Professor Babagana Zulum, Governor of Borno State; Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri, Governor of Adamawa State; and Mai Mala Buni, Governor of Yobe State
a710.name: Professor Babagana Zulum
a710.title: Governor of Borno State; Ahmadu Umaru Fintiri, Governor of Adamawa State; and Mai Mala Buni, Governor of Yobe State
a710.speech: In their remarks, reaffirmed their commitment to sustaining collaboration with the UN and partners to address pressing humanitarian needs and foster sustainable development.

a710.speaker: Report distributed by the APO Group on behalf of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a710.name: Report distributed by the APO Group on behalf of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a710.speech: Stated that urgent funding and resources are required from donors and the Government to ensure that food and nutrition assistance and other urgent support is provided to people in critical need.

a773.speaker: Suleiman Kyababa, chairman of NASCAM (Namibian Society of Composers and Authors of Music)
a773.name: Suleiman Kyababa
a773.title: chairman of NASCAM (Namibian Society of Composers and Authors of Music)
a773.speech: Reported on the results of the annual general meeting of 5 April, an important point being the presentation of a draft of the audited financial reports for 2024, with the final audit and approval to take place at a special general meeting on 2 August.

a773.speaker: Suleiman Kyababa, chairman of NASCAM
a773.name: Suleiman Kyababa
a773.title: chairman of NASCAM
a773.speech: Announced that the board election had been postponed because there were too few nominations, and noted that a stricter selection process for the board had been presented, part of which consists of psychometric assessments and written tests ; emphasised that the measures correspond to international standards in the creative sector and are already part of NASCAM’s regulatory framework.

a773.speaker: Some NASCAM members
a773.name: Some NASCAM members
a773.speech: Expressed concerns, because they feel that this approach is not based on the constitution.

a773.speaker: NASCAM (press conference)
a773.name: NASCAM (press conference)
a773.speech: Released the figures of the royalty distribution from the last payment cycle: the society paid out approximately N$917,000 to local rights holders, while international royalty transfers amount to approximately N$411,000 for societies with reciprocal agreements and approximately N$590,000 for societies without formal ties; the five largest royalty recipients among the local payouts were also announced, with the member with the highest earnings receiving approximately N$33,000.

a801.speaker: Dr Blazio Manobo, director for Strategic Policy Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation in the Zimbabwean Ministry of Youth Empowerment, Development and Vocational Training
a801.name: Dr Blazio Manobo
a801.title: director for Strategic Policy Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation in the Zimbabwean Ministry of Youth Empowerment, Development and Vocational Training
a801.speech: Confirmed the initiative to finalise a comprehensive Youth Empowerment Strategy ; "We have gone right round the country making consultations with the youth. This document, which we aim to finalize by the end of May, will serve as a national blueprint for youth empowerment, ensuring that no young person is left behind" ; "The youth have made it clear: whatever you do without consulting them is not for them. This time, they are fully on board. Their inputs have shaped the strategy, and their energy will drive its implementation"

a801.speaker: Dr Blazio Manobo, director for Strategic Policy Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation, Ministry of Youth Empowerment
a801.name: Dr Blazio Manobo
a801.title: director for Strategic Policy Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation, Ministry of Youth Empowerment
a801.speech: Said the strategy will be presented to a thematic working group comprising government Ministries, Non-Governmental Organisations and United Nations agencies for validation before being submitted to the Cabinet for approval; he said once adopted, it will become the guiding document for youth-focused initiatives, ensuring coherence and alignment with the National Development Strategy 2 (NDS2) and the broader Vision 2030 agenda.

a801.speaker: Dr Blazio Manobo, director for Strategic Policy Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation, Ministry of Youth Empowerment
a801.name: Dr Blazio Manobo
a801.title: director for Strategic Policy Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation, Ministry of Youth Empowerment
a801.speech: "These are the ones loitering, susceptible to drug and substance abuse. This is a dangerous situation because they are not adding value to the country or contributing to the GDP. President Mnangagwa has been clear that we must not leave anyone behind. Our goal is to reach out to these idle youths and ensure they participate meaningfully in national development." ; "We want to make sure that as we carry out youth empowerment, every young person can access some money. Whether through entrepreneurship, vocational training, or formal employment, we are committed to unlocking their potential"

a801.speaker: Emmerson Mnangagwa, President of Zimbabwe (cited by Dr Blazio Manobo)
a801.name: Emmerson Mnangagwa
a801.title: President of Zimbabwe (cited by Dr Blazio Manobo)
a801.speech: "President Mnangagwa has been clear that we must not leave anyone behind."

a1178.speaker: Inigo Montoya, character/actor in the film The Princess Bride
a1178.name: Inigo Montoya
a1178.title: character/actor in the film The Princess Bride
a1178.speech: In a conversation with a co-actor in the film The Princess Bride, Montoya says: "You keep using that word, 'nice,' in connection with Donald Trump. I do not think you know what that word means." ; "Trump is utterly devoid of anything even resembling empathy or consideration for his fellow man. He is morally bankrupt and self-absorbed to a fault. He is also a malignant narcissist." ; "Trump is never too busy to exploit another person's weaknesses or take gratuitous advantage of someone's misfortune. If you look up the word inhumane in the dictionary, you will find his picture." ; "Trump cleaves to the old adage, 'no man stands so tall as when he stoops to kneel on the neck of a black person.'"

a1178.speaker: Nate White, articulate and witty writer from England
a1178.name: Nate White
a1178.title: articulate and witty writer from England
a1178.speech: Asked about why some British people do not like Donald Trump, wrote: "A few things spring to mind. Trump lacks certain qualities which the British traditionally esteem. For instance, he has no class, no charm, no coolness, no credibility, no compassion, no wit, no warmth, no wisdom, no subtlety, no sensitivity, no self-awareness, no humility, no honour and no grace - all qualities, funnily enough, with which his predecessor Mr. [Barrack] Obama was generously blessed. So for us, the stark contrast does rather throw Trump's limitations into embarrassingly sharp relief." ; "Plus, we like a laugh. And while Trump may be laughable, he has never once said anything wry, witty or even faintly amusing - not once, ever... And that fact is particularly disturbing to the British sensibility - for us, to lack humour is almost inhuman... He doesn't even seem to understand what a joke is - his idea of a joke is a crass comment, an illiterate insult, a casual act of cruelty." ; "Trump is a troll. And like all trolls, he is never funny and he never laughs; he only crows or jeers. And scarily, he doesn't just talk in crude, witless insults - he actually thinks in them. His mind is a simple bot-like algorithm of petty prejudices and knee-jerk nastiness." ; "There is never any under-layer of irony, complexity, nuance or depth. It's all surface... We see it as having no inner world, no soul. And in Britain we traditionally side with David, not Goliath. All our heroes are plucky underdogs: Robin Hood, Dick Whittington, Oliver Twist. Trump is neither plucky, nor an underdog... He's more a fat white slug. A Jabba the Hutt of privilege." ; "And worse, he is that most unforgivable of all things to the British: a bully. That is, except when he is among bullies; then he suddenly transforms into a snivelling sidekick instead. There are unspoken rules to this stuff - the Queensberry rules of basic decency - and he breaks them all. He punches downwards - which a gentleman should, would, could never do - and every blow he aims is below the belt. He particularly likes to kick the vulnerable or voiceless - and he kicks them when they are down."

a1438.speaker: Joaquim Mangrasse, Head of Mozambique's Armed Forces
a1438.name: Joaquim Mangrasse
a1438.title: Head of Mozambique's Armed Forces
a1438.speech: "This mission will contribute to operations to defend Mozambique. After finishing the training, we will prepare an operational training plan for the future. The soldiers trained here will be able to go on missions," said in Maputo.

a1438.speaker: European Council (decision of 19 November 2021)
a1438.name: European Council (decision of 19 November 2021)
a1438.speech: adopted a decision establishing a 40 million euro assistance measure under the European Peace Facility (EPF) in support of Mozambique, complementing an urgent measure amounting to 4 million euros approved under the EPF on 30 July 2021 for the most urgently required equipment; the EU will support the Mozambican military units trained by EUTM Mozambique and enable them to conduct security operations in Cabo Delgado, providing adequate, non-lethal equipment including individual and collective equipment, ground mobility assets, technical tools and a field hospital, subject to compliance with international human rights and humanitarian law.

a1438.speaker: Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Mozambique (letter of 27 August 2021)
a1438.name: Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Mozambique (letter of 27 August 2021)
a1438.speech: requested the assistance, in her letter of 27 August 2021 to the High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, which the November 19 decision follows.

a1438.speaker: Reports (unnamed)
a1438.name: Reports (unnamed)
a1438.speech: According to reports, the European Union (EU) concretely sent 1,100 soldiers to the country in September and the troops will be in Mozambique for two years to train rapid intervention units.

a1438.speaker: Reports (unnamed)
a1438.name: Reports (unnamed)
a1438.speech: Reports said that Islamic-State linked militants have been wreaking havoc in the area since 2017, raiding villages and towns in violence that has claimed at least 3,340 lives and displaced more than 800,000 people.

a1442.speaker: Morocco (government position)
a1442.name: Morocco (government position)
a1442.speech: calls for the relaunch of the peace process between Israel and Hamas; frequently restates its position as the kingdom continues to receive criticism, notably from local activists opposed to the country's decision to restore its ties with Israel in December 2020.

a1442.speaker: Omar Hilale, Permanent Ambassador of Morocco to the UN
a1442.name: Omar Hilale
a1442.title: Permanent Ambassador of Morocco to the UN
a1442.speech: reiterated the country's satisfaction with the ceasefire agreement between Hamas and Israel, speaking on Monday in New York during a meeting devoted to the situation in the Middle East, notably in Palestine; described the ceasefire as a decisive step forward for the reconstruction of what was destroyed by the disastrous and genocidal Israeli campaign launched in October 2023 ; "The ceasefire agreement should pave the way for the reconstruction of what was destroyed by the war, as well as for the launch of a genuine peace process, allowing the establishment of a Palestinian State within the 1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as its capital, living side by side and in peace with Israel," he declared before the Security Council ; noted that Morocco welcomes the progress made towards halting hostilities and attacks on civilians, hoping that the ceasefire agreement will be fully respected through the release of hostages and detainees and the return of displaced persons ; recalled King Mohammed VI's commitment to the Palestinian cause, adding that his defence of this position has been constant and clear given that the creation of a Palestinian State is the cornerstone of peace and stability in the Middle East ; "Gaza must be an integral part of the independent Palestinian territories, where legal and political jurisdiction belongs to the Palestinian National Authority," he declared, adding that the continuation of unilateral Israeli acts in Al Quds exacerbates tensions.

a1442.speaker: Qatar
a1442.name: Qatar
a1442.speech: echoed Morocco's call, reiterating the need to respect the ceasefire in Gaza; also called for the adoption of a binding resolution supporting the full implementation of the ceasefire.

a1449.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a1449.name: World Health Organisation (WHO)
a1449.speech: has called for the immediate global rollout of a breakthrough HIV drug, lenacapavir (LEN), that only requires two injections per year to offer near-total protection against HIV and the development of AIDS; emphasised the urgent need to make LEN widely accessible, through pharmacies, clinics, and online consultations, especially as global HIV prevention efforts are faltering; also recommended rapid HIV testing over more complex and costly methods; urged governments, donors, and partners to incorporate it into national HIV prevention programmes without delay.

a1449.speaker: Tedros Ghebreyesus, WHO Director-General
a1449.name: Tedros Ghebreyesus
a1449.title: WHO Director-General
a1449.speech: hailed lenacapavir as "the next best thing" in HIV prevention, given the absence of an effective vaccine; while speaking on Monday during the 13th International AIDS Society (IAS 2025) Conference on HIV Science, in Kigali, Rwanda, said lenacapavir has been shown in trials to prevent almost all HIV infections among at-risk populations.

a1449.speaker: World Health Organisation (WHO) data
a1449.name: World Health Organisation (WHO) data
a1449.speech: According to WHO, 1.3 million people were newly infected with HIV in 2024, with the most affected groups being sex workers, men who have sex with men, transgender people, people who inject drugs, prison populations, and young people.

a1449.speaker: Meg Doherty, Director of WHO's Global HIV, Hepatitis, and STI Programmes
a1449.name: Meg Doherty
a1449.title: Director of WHO's Global HIV, Hepatitis, and STI Programmes
a1449.speech: "We have the tools and the knowledge to end AIDS." ; "What we need now is bold implementation of these recommendations, grounded in equity and powered by communities."

a1465.speaker: United Nations Children's Fund (Unicef)
a1465.name: United Nations Children's Fund (Unicef)
a1465.speech: says the recent reduction in official development assistance (ODA) is a concern as it threatens to limit access to safety nets ; in its highlight of the 2025/26 Citizens Budget also warned of deepening existing vulnerabilities considering that 75 percent of ODA is financing expenditures in social sectors such as health, education, humanitarian and social infrastructure.

a1465.speaker: Unicef (highlight of the 2025/26 Citizens Budget)
a1465.name: Unicef (highlight of the 2025/26 Citizens Budget)
a1465.speech: "Against this background, Unicef, therefore, encourages the government to explore innovative financing options to support continued delivery of key social services, including social protection programmes to help cushion the most vulnerable against frequent shocks and rising price levels."

a1465.speaker: Unicef
a1465.name: Unicef
a1465.speech: According to Unicef, Malawi continues to face persistent macroeconomic challenges and weather-related shocks that have negatively affected the country's economic growth ; "[This] indicate continued declining per capita income for Malawi, deepening poverty and inequality amongst households."

a1465.speaker: Treasury (Malawi)
a1465.name: Treasury (Malawi)
a1465.speech: projects the economy to rebound from 1.8 percent in 2024 to 3.2 percent in 2025.

a1465.speaker: International Monetary Fund and World Bank (growth projections)
a1465.name: International Monetary Fund and World Bank (growth projections)
a1465.speech: gross domestic product growth projections by the International Monetary Fund (2.4 percent) and World Bank (two percent) for 2025 show reduced growth.

a1465.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB) data
a1465.name: African Development Bank (AfDB) data
a1465.speech: show that Malawi's actual disbursements have fallen short by 61.8 percent of the target in the 2024/25 financial year, following aid cut and US tariff impositions.

a1465.speaker: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a1465.name: African Development Bank (AfDB)
a1465.speech: The bank said this is compounded by the suspension of $350 million annual funding from the United States Agency for International Development (USAid), the cancellation of the $350 million five-year Millennium Challenge Corporation support and the imposition of an 18 percent tariff on exports from Malawi to the USA.

a1465.speaker: Simplex Chithyola-Banda, Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
a1465.name: Simplex Chithyola-Banda
a1465.title: Minister of Finance and Economic Affairs
a1465.speech: projected grants at K1.17 trillion in the 2024/25 National Budget, of which K1.10 trillion was expected from international organisations and K72.69 billion from foreign governments.

a1465.speaker: Lingalireni Mihowa, Oxfam in Malawi country director
a1465.name: Lingalireni Mihowa
a1465.title: Oxfam in Malawi country director
a1465.speech: indicated that in the face of economic distress and humanitarian shocks, restructuring the social protection programmes to move from just consumption is key. She said: "It is important to protect the most vulnerable and poor yes, but there is also need to design the programmes that have exit strategies, have sustainability pathways and those that are linked to production and stimulating local economies, not just consumption." ; "There is need to limit consumption to marginalised groups who cannot offer labour for cash like the elderly and children so that we generate input for the economy while supporting production."

a1465.speaker: Williams Banda, Treasury spokesperson
a1465.name: Williams Banda
a1465.title: Treasury spokesperson
a1465.speech: earlier said only K9.2 billion of USAid funding appeared in the 2024/25 National Budget, but that the US government off-budget projection in FY2024/25 was about K307 billion.

a1465.speaker: Ministry of Gender, Community Development and Social Welfare
a1465.name: Ministry of Gender
a1465.title: Community Development and Social Welfare
a1465.speech: which spearheads social cash transfer hopes to increase its coverage to 15 percent between 2022 and 2027 through the SCTP Strategic Plan 2022/27 ; Ministry of Gender anticipated [the 0.11 percent of the national budget devoted to social assistance] to fall further.

a1654.speaker: European Union (Brussels)
a1654.name: European Union (Brussels)
a1654.speech: said the change requiring all new smartphones, tablets and cameras to use the same charger will cut costs and waste ; has said the single charger rule will simplify the life of Europeans and slash costs for consumers, and argued that by allowing consumers to purchase a new device without a new charger, it will also reduce the mountain of obsolete chargers.

a1654.speaker: European Parliament (post on social media X)
a1654.name: European Parliament (post on social media X)
a1654.speech: "Starting today, all new mobile phones, tablets, digital cameras, headphones, speakers, keyboards and many other electronics sold in the EU will have to be equipped with a USB Type-C charging port." ; "Regardless of manufacturer. Benefitting your wallet and the environment."

a1654.speaker: Apple
a1654.name: Apple
a1654.speech: said in 2021 that such regulation "stifles innovation", but by September last year it had begun shipping phones with the new port ; refused to abide by the earlier voluntary single charging norm agreed with the European Commission and ditch its Lightning ports.

a1654.speaker: European Commission
a1654.name: European Commission
a1654.speech: said at the time of the law's approval that it was expected to save at least 200 million euros ($208 million) per year and cut more than a thousand tonnes of EU electronic waste every year.

a1654.speaker: European Commission (post on X)
a1654.name: European Commission (post on X)
a1654.speech: "It's time for THE charger." ; "It means better-charging technology, reduced e-waste, and less fuss to find the chargers you need."

a1746.speaker: Internal memo cited by AFP
a1746.name: Internal memo cited by AFP
a1746.speech: States that the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), led by billionaire Elon Musk, will impose "significant reductions" in the number of staff and programmes of the Millennium Challenge Corporation.

a1746.speaker: Politico (US news site)
a1746.name: Politico (US news site)
a1746.speech: Reports that the agency is expected to dismiss its 320 employees and end grants to about 40 developing countries where it has projects.

a1746.speaker: Acting CEO of the MCC (e-mail to all staff, cited by Politico)
a1746.name: Acting CEO of the MCC (e-mail to all staff
a1746.title: cited by Politico)
a1746.speech: Says in an e-mail sent to all staff on Tuesday that he learned from the DOGE team that there will soon be a significant reduction in the number of the agency's programmes and, consequently, in its staff.

a1746.speaker: MCC leadership (all-staff meeting)
a1746.name: MCC leadership (all-staff meeting)
a1746.speech: Told employees at an all-staff meeting held this morning that DOGE would draft a resolution next week for the agency's board - made up of Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, the acting CEO and four private-sector members - to close grants worldwide in the coming months.

a1746.speaker: Participant in the MCC meeting (anonymous), speaking to Politico
a1746.name: Participant in the MCC meeting (anonymous)
a1746.title: speaking to Politico
a1746.speech: Told Politico on condition of anonymity about the planned board resolution, adding that the expectation is that within 90 days all MCC operations will be shut down.

a1746.speaker: US State Department (reorganisation announced Tuesday)
a1746.name: US State Department (reorganisation announced Tuesday)
a1746.speech: Announced a reorganisation that includes the abolition of the division for "civilian security, democracy and human rights", which will be replaced by another responsible for "coordination of foreign assistance and humanitarian affairs", expected to absorb what remains of USAID.

a1746.speaker: Ministry of Finance of Cabo Verde (data)
a1746.name: Ministry of Finance of Cabo Verde (data)
a1746.speech: According to Ministry of Finance data, Cabo Verde benefited from its first MCC compact in July 2005, when the Government and the American agency signed a five-year, $110 million agreement to help increase the country's economic growth and reduce poverty through investments in infrastructure, watershed management and support to agriculture, and private sector development.

a1785.speaker: Unidentified caller (suspected French intelligence agent), speaking to the author by WhatsApp
a1785.name: Unidentified caller (suspected French intelligence agent)
a1785.title: speaking to the author by WhatsApp
a1785.speech: Asked the author what he was currently doing: "How are your affairs going?" "What are you doing at present?" "Where do you stand with your projects?" ; and offered: "We can help you with your project!" ; then specified: "The factory manufacturing irrigation pipes for precision agriculture. With my colleagues, we are going to organise a meeting to talk about it."

a1785.speaker: Anonymous source who contacted the author three months later
a1785.name: Anonymous source who contacted the author three months later
a1785.speech: Told the author that the group wanted to take advantage of his "not very glowing situation" and to request his help in their "subversive projects", in exchange guaranteeing him "lodging, a wife, money, exile"; but that they were in no way surprised by his reaction: "They knew they had a patriot in front of them; they found instead a chauvinist," concluded the source.

a1785.speaker: General Charles de Gaulle (quotation often attributed to him)
a1785.name: General Charles de Gaulle (quotation often attributed to him)
a1785.speech: "France has interests, France has no friends!"

a1785.speaker: The only person to whom the author told the story (postscript)
a1785.name: The only person to whom the author told the story (postscript)
a1785.speech: "Why do you give up your interests for the benefit of those people when they profit from the Republic? Besides, you have not criticised this Transition regime, whereas we remember your salvos against all the past governments!"

a1785.speaker: Abdou Karim Dramé, independent journalist/consultant, analyst of sustainable-development issues and innovations, researcher on accelerated growth strategies (open letter to President Assimi Goïta)
a1785.name: Abdou Karim Dramé
a1785.title: independent journalist/consultant, analyst of sustainable-development issues and innovations, researcher on accelerated growth strategies (open letter to President Assimi Goïta)
a1785.speech: Wrote that he refused to collaborate with the "foreign agents", putting Mali's interests before his own, out of loyalty to the Fatherland of Mali ; argued that France resorts to all forms of subversion — support for separatist rebels, the instrumentalisation, financing and training of terrorist groups, political and economic interference — to install a regime favourable to it at the head of Mali, and that what is not normal is that Malians accept being plundered, robbed and dominated by France ; estimated Mali's development financing needs at 20 billion US dollars over the next five years and urged the country to turn to the major sovereign wealth funds and investment capital.

a1884.speaker: Elon Musk, tech billionaire and former head of Doge
a1884.name: Elon Musk
a1884.title: tech billionaire and former head of Doge
a1884.speech: hit out at President Donald Trump's signature tax and spending bill, describing it as a “disgusting abomination”; posted on X that the bill would add to the US budget deficit and saddle Americans with “crushing” debt; said the “outrageous, pork-filled” spending bill will “massively increase the already gigantic budget deficit to $2.5 trillion (!!!) and burden America [sic] citizens with crushingly unsustainable debt” ; “Shame on those who voted for it” ; “In November next year, we fire all politicians who betrayed the American people”; he had previously called the plan “disappointing”.

a1884.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1884.name: Donald Trump
a1884.title: US President
a1884.speech: said of Musk's departure that “he will, always, be with us, helping all the way”.

a1884.speaker: Karoline Leavitt, White House press secretary
a1884.name: Karoline Leavitt
a1884.title: White House press secretary
a1884.speech: said “the President already knows where Elon Musk stood on this bill” ; “This is one, big, beautiful bill. And he's sticking to it.”

a1884.speaker: Rand Paul, Kentucky Senator
a1884.name: Rand Paul
a1884.title: Kentucky Senator
a1884.speech: has said over the last few days he will not support the bill if it raises the debt ceiling: “The GOP [the Republican Party] will own the debt once they vote for this,” he told CBS News.

a1884.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a1884.name: Donald Trump
a1884.title: US President
a1884.speech: responded to Paul with a series of social media posts, accusing him of having “very little understanding of the bill” and saying that the “people of Kentucky can't stand him” ; “His ideas are actually crazy.”

a1884.speaker: John Thune, Senate majority leader
a1884.name: John Thune
a1884.title: Senate majority leader
a1884.speech: told reporters the party plans to “proceed full speed ahead” despite “a difference of opinion”: “We have an agenda that everybody campaigned on, most notably the president.”

a1884.speaker: Mike Johnson, Republican Speaker of the House
a1884.name: Mike Johnson
a1884.title: Republican Speaker of the House
a1884.speech: told reporters on Capitol Hill that “my friend Elon is terribly wrong” ; “It's a very important first start. Elon is missing it”; he said he had a 20-minute phone call with the tycoon about the bill on Monday, adding that its phasing out of electric vehicle tax credits could “have an effect” on Tesla, Musk's firm: “I lament that” ; “I just deeply regret he's made this mistake.”

a1884.speaker: Axios (report cited)
a1884.name: Axios (report cited)
a1884.speech: According to Axios, among the issues that upset Musk was air traffic control at the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA): Musk was hoping it would be run on his Starlink satellite system, but he was denied because of issues relating to the technology and the appearance of a conflict of interest.

a1884.speaker: Chuck Schumer, Senate Minority Leader
a1884.name: Chuck Schumer
a1884.title: Senate Minority Leader
a1884.speech: said: “Even Elon Musk, who's been part of the whole process, and is one of Trump's buddies, said the bill is bad. We can imagine how bad this bill is.”

a2015.speaker: Emmanuel Kabore, technical director of the PREPARE-Burkina Project
a2015.name: Emmanuel Kabore
a2015.title: technical director of the PREPARE-Burkina Project
a2015.speech: Indicated that the project’s areas of intervention are family planning, reproductive health, maternal, newborn and child health, nutrition, water, hygiene and sanitation ; “We want to make communities the actors of their own development. It will involve finding innovative and home-grown solutions together.”

a2015.speaker: Emmanuel Kabore, technical director of the PREPARE-Burkina Project
a2015.name: Emmanuel Kabore
a2015.title: technical director of the PREPARE-Burkina Project
a2015.speech: Said the project will make it possible to strengthen the links between community health services and professional health structures, to improve disaster management and response, and to strengthen the autonomy and engagement of young people; he noted that PREPARE-Burkina is a very particular project ; “There will be better coordination and synergy of interventions, with, upstream, the duty of accountability to local authorities and to the various communities that are stakeholders in the implementation of this project” ; consultation frameworks will be organised in order to better capitalise on the various interventions, and the project’s principle is “to support what already exists in order to avoid any duplication”.

a2015.speaker: Emmanuel Kabore, technical director of the PREPARE-Burkina Project
a2015.name: Emmanuel Kabore
a2015.title: technical director of the PREPARE-Burkina Project
a2015.speech: Urged actors in the Eastern region to support his team for a successful implementation of the programme.

a2015.speaker: Hamidou Sore, secretary-general of the Eastern region
a2015.name: Hamidou Sore
a2015.title: secretary-general of the Eastern region
a2015.speech: Said this project brings answers to the concerns of the people of the East, an area severely tested by insecurity with its corollary of mass displacement; he expressed his gratitude to the American people for this new project which, according to him, is the symbol of the “fruitful” cooperation between the United States of America and Burkina Faso.

a2015.speaker: Aly Diallo, first vice-president of the Eastern regional council
a2015.name: Aly Diallo
a2015.title: first vice-president of the Eastern regional council
a2015.speech: Expressed the wish that this “fine example” of development cooperation be perpetuated.

a2015.speaker: PREPARE-Burkina Project (stated objective)
a2015.name: PREPARE-Burkina Project (stated objective)
a2015.speech: Its stated objective is to “create shock-resistant communities by proposing a new compact between them and their health services.”

a2350.speaker: Expression of Interest (EOI) published by the Eswatini Public Procurement Regulatory Agency (ESPPRA)
a2350.name: Expression of Interest (EOI) published by the Eswatini Public Procurement Regulatory Agency (ESPPRA)
a2350.speech: Explained that this exercise aims to optimise capex spend, prioritise projects aligned with the corporate strategy, and establish a tariff structure and methodology that supports equitable and sustainable service delivery across urban and rural areas.

a2350.speaker: Expression of Interest (EOI) published by the Eswatini Public Procurement Regulatory Agency (ESPPRA)
a2350.name: Expression of Interest (EOI) published by the Eswatini Public Procurement Regulatory Agency (ESPPRA)
a2350.speech: Mentioned that the corporation, led by Jabulile Mashwama as Managing Director, currently maintains a total of 77,265 active customer accounts, segmented into four primary categories: government (2,185), corporate (3,557), commercial (4,029) and residential, which it stated is the largest category at 67,494. Stated that the corporation total revenue was projected at E590 million, with residential customers contributing approximately 37 percent, government 29 percent, corporate 18 percent and commercial 16 percent, and that monthly the corporation issues bills totalling approximately E48 million.

a2350.speaker: Expression of Interest (EOI) published by the Eswatini Public Procurement Regulatory Agency (ESPPRA)
a2350.name: Expression of Interest (EOI) published by the Eswatini Public Procurement Regulatory Agency (ESPPRA)
a2350.speech: Stated that as of year ended 31 March 2025 total outstanding debt stood at E272 million, a decrease of E13 million or five percent on the E284 million recorded on 31 March 2024, that the collections ratio was 109 percent against a target of 115 percent, and that debtor days remained high at 172 days: "The target remains at 70 days. By customer category, the government segment held E75 million in outstanding debt. Corporate debt stood at E18 million, while commercial customers owed E23 million. The residential category remains the largest contributor to outstanding debt, with a balance of E155 million."

a2455.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, Senegalese President
a2455.name: Bassirou Diomaye Faye
a2455.title: Senegalese President
a2455.speech: In calling for early elections, Faye said he wants a comfortable majority to be able to enact the deep reforms he promised when elected to the top job in March.

a2455.speaker: National Electoral Commission of Senegal (official results), confirmed by the Constitutional Council
a2455.name: National Electoral Commission of Senegal (official results)
a2455.title: confirmed by the Constitutional Council
a2455.speech: According to the official results of the National Electoral Commission and confirmed by the Constitutional Council, Pastef won 130 of the 165 seats at stake.

a2455.speaker: Bassirou Diomaye Faye, Senegalese President
a2455.name: Bassirou Diomaye Faye
a2455.title: Senegalese President
a2455.speech: While in Mbour, he stated that "the government is working hard to implement adequate policies to give jobs to young people here in Senegal and invite them to rebuild our country".

a2455.speaker: Human rights groups such as Amnesty International
a2455.name: Human rights groups such as Amnesty International
a2455.speech: According to human rights groups such as Amnesty International, the law establishes impunity for human rights violations and is an insult to victims of mass demonstrations that took place in Senegal between 2021 and 2023, during which more than 60 people were killed by the armed forces.

a2455.speaker: National statistics agency of Senegal
a2455.name: National statistics agency of Senegal
a2455.speech: About 75 percent of Senegal's population is under 35, and the overall unemployment rate topped 23 percent in the first quarter of 2024, according to the national statistics agency.

a2455.speaker: Ousmane Sonko, Senegalese Prime Minister
a2455.name: Ousmane Sonko
a2455.title: Senegalese Prime Minister
a2455.speech: Following a review carried out in the early months of Faye's presidency, Sonko in September accused the former government of falsifying these figures, especially regarding the country's debt.

a2455.speaker: Senegalese media
a2455.name: Senegalese media
a2455.speech: Senegalese media reported earlier in November that the International Monetary Fund had decided to suspend its payments to Dakar until a review was completed.

a2486.speaker: Randy Berry, United States Ambassador to Namibia
a2486.name: Randy Berry
a2486.title: United States Ambassador to Namibia
a2486.speech: Shared the sentiments that the volunteers' roles are crucial in strengthening communities and addressing critical issues like HIV, particularly in areas where health behavior and support are needed ; "I would like to express my deepest gratitude to the Namibian government, particularly the Ministry of Health and Social Services, for your continued partnership and support of the Peace Corps Mission and joint important work through the U.S. President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR)."

a2486.speaker: Dr. Utjiua Muinjangue, Deputy Minister of Health and Social Services of Namibia
a2486.name: Dr. Utjiua Muinjangue
a2486.title: Deputy Minister of Health and Social Services of Namibia
a2486.speech: Stated that Namibia's sustainable development agenda is anchored in transformative frameworks aimed at fostering inclusive economic growth and improving the quality of life for all citizens.

a2486.speaker: Dr. Utjiua Muinjangue, Deputy Minister of Health and Social Services of Namibia
a2486.name: Dr. Utjiua Muinjangue
a2486.title: Deputy Minister of Health and Social Services of Namibia
a2486.speech: Commended the US government for assisting Namibia's plans through the US President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief: "HIV infections in Namibia have reduced by an extraordinary 65% between 2004 and 2022, reflecting the effectiveness of targeted interventions and comprehensive health strategies."

a2867.speaker: Venezuelan prosecutors (public prosecutor's office)
a2867.name: Venezuelan prosecutors (public prosecutor's office)
a2867.speech: Said Saturday that “Citizen Edmundo Gonzalez Urrutia” is summoned “on August 26 at 10 am for an interview”, as part of an investigation into the opposition's publishing of electoral records

a2867.speaker: Tarek William Saab, Venezuelan Attorney General
a2867.name: Tarek William Saab
a2867.title: Venezuelan Attorney General
a2867.speech: Had foreshadowed the summoning Friday, saying Gonzalez Urrutia would have to explain his “disobedience”; said the opposition's website, where it has posted a detailed breakdown of election results, had “usurped” the powers of the Maduro-aligned CNE electoral council

a2867.speaker: Maria Corina Machado, Venezuelan opposition leader (post on X)
a2867.name: Maria Corina Machado
a2867.title: Venezuelan opposition leader (post on X)
a2867.speech: Was defiant, calling in a post on X for Venezuelans to take to the streets again on Wednesday. “One month after our glorious victory, in which Edmundo Gonzalez was elected President, Venezuelans again take to the streets,” she said, calling for supporters to come “with family, with your children, with your grandchildren and with your voting record in hand”

a2867.speaker: CNE (Venezuelan National Electoral Council)
a2867.name: CNE (Venezuelan National Electoral Council)
a2867.speech: Declared Maduro the winner of the July 28 election with 52 percent of votes cast, but has refused to publish detailed results, claiming hackers had corrupted the data

a2867.speaker: Observer mission from the US-based Carter Center
a2867.name: Observer mission from the US-based Carter Center
a2867.speech: Said there was no evidence of a cyber attack

a2867.speaker: Edmundo Gonzalez Urrutia, Venezuelan opposition candidate
a2867.name: Edmundo Gonzalez Urrutia
a2867.title: Venezuelan opposition candidate
a2867.speech: Refused to attend the Supreme Court hearings, saying doing so would risk his freedom

a2867.speaker: Maria Corina Machado, Venezuelan opposition leader (Fox News interview)
a2867.name: Maria Corina Machado
a2867.title: Venezuelan opposition leader (Fox News interview)
a2867.speech: Said in a televised Fox News interview on Saturday that Maduro had unleashed a brutal “campaign of terror”; she pledged to “keep on fighting, peacefully protesting, increasing pressure domestically and internationally, until Maduro understands that his best option is to accept the terms of a negotiation that would bring us to a transition to democracy”; she has demanded that Maduro enter into transition negotiations

a2867.speaker: Nicolas Maduro, President of Venezuela
a2867.name: Nicolas Maduro
a2867.title: President of Venezuela
a2867.speech: Has called for the arrest of Gonzalez Urrutia and has rejected outright the demand that he enter into transition negotiations

a2867.speaker: Venezuela's Supreme Court
a2867.name: Venezuela's Supreme Court
a2867.speech: On Thursday certified Maduro's reelection to a third, six-year term, and reprimanded Gonzalez Urrutia for not appearing as ordered

a2867.speaker: Presidents of Brazil and Colombia (joint statement)
a2867.name: Presidents of Brazil and Colombia (joint statement)
a2867.speech: Issued a joint statement on Saturday reiterating a call for the CNE to release detailed vote results, while saying they “take note” of the Supreme Court ruling. “Both presidents remain convinced that the credibility of the electoral process can only be restored through the transparent publication of disaggregated and verifiable data”

a2867.speaker: Josep Borrell, EU's top diplomat
a2867.name: Josep Borrell
a2867.title: EU's top diplomat
a2867.speech: Reiterated on Saturday that the CNE is the Venezuelan “body legally and constitutionally responsible” for publishing results. “Only complete and independently verifiable results will be accepted and recognized to ensure that the will of the Venezuelan people is respected” ; “The Venezuelan people have to decide their own destiny. Their will must prevail.”

a3000.speaker: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Cooperation and Moroccans Residing Abroad of Morocco (press statement)
a3000.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a3000.title: African Cooperation and Moroccans Residing Abroad of Morocco (press statement)
a3000.speech: Indicated on Monday that, as a testimony of the permanent support and tangible solidarity of King Mohammed VI, President of the Al-Quds Committee, towards the brotherly Palestinian people, the Sovereign had given his very high instructions for the dispatch of additional humanitarian aid for the benefit of the inhabitants of Gaza; specified that this aid consists of approximately 100 tonnes of foodstuffs and medicines, specifically intended for vulnerable groups, particularly children and infants; concluded that this generous Royal initiative reflects the King's constant concern about the critical humanitarian situation experienced by the population of Gaza, as well as the Sovereign's unwavering commitment to alleviating their suffering.

a3000.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco, President of the Al-Quds Committee
a3000.name: King Mohammed VI of Morocco
a3000.title: President of the Al-Quds Committee
a3000.speech: Gave his very high instructions for the dispatch of additional humanitarian aid to the inhabitants of Gaza, and insisted that this humanitarian aid should, like the previous consignments, be transported by aircraft and delivered urgently and directly to the beneficiaries among the Palestinian brothers.

a3363.speaker: Josiah F. Joekai Jr., Director-General of the Civil Service Agency (CSA) of Liberia
a3363.name: Josiah F. Joekai Jr.
a3363.title: Director-General of the Civil Service Agency (CSA) of Liberia
a3363.speech: Has threatened to dismiss vocal civil servants without fear; according to Joekai, the CSA will not condone acts of disorderly conduct and will not resist firing unbecoming conduct, disrespectful civil servants in keeping with job policies under the Civil Service Standing Order: "We have to have employees who are respectful, respect for each other, respect for their leaders, respectful of themselves, and people that our country can rely on." ; said civil servants who do not fall in line and act contrary will be booted out ; warned the LACRA employees, cautioning them not to be disrespectful to their leaders and denigrate the government they served: "We cannot have employees spreading lies, disinformation, undermining, and denigrating the image of this government." ; "Where you will sit, spread lies and destroy the very government they serve, and there is no policy that says we must keep them, no." ; referencing the nine employees of the Monrovia City Corporation (MCC) allegedly illegally dismissed in August 2024: "When few employees of MCC took to social media and spread lies about the government, we took action and dismissed them. We cannot have employees denigrating the image of the government, and be protected, and in as much the government has the social responsibility to the economic needs of the people, to provide jobs, but we will not condom disorderly conducts, it is unacceptable in keeping with our laws and policies. And we will penalize employees, without fear, in keeping with the Civil Service Standing order, and I, as Director-General of the CSA, will ensure there is decency in the Civil Service of Liberia."

a3363.speaker: Josiah F. Joekai Jr., Director-General of the Civil Service Agency (CSA) of Liberia
a3363.name: Josiah F. Joekai Jr.
a3363.title: Director-General of the Civil Service Agency (CSA) of Liberia
a3363.speech: Vows to investigate and dismiss the employees of LACRA who protested against the leadership of Christopher Sankolo if facts are not shown in their complaints: "The things that are said here, are not things people should just say loosely," adding, "I'm not saying they are not facts, but when they are documented- We will look into it, and make sure, they are speaking the facts, otherwise, the situation will be treated base on the provisions of the standing order that guides all of us." ; immediately instructed LACRA Boss Sankolo to submit a formal communication complaining the protesting staff for onward investigation.

a3363.speaker: Aggrieved employees of the Liberia Agricultural Commodity Regulatory Authority (LACRA)
a3363.name: Aggrieved employees of the Liberia Agricultural Commodity Regulatory Authority (LACRA)
a3363.speech: Protested and rampaged the entity's premises on Tuesday, demanding accountability of revenues generated by the administration from April 2023 to March 2024; they also cited corruption and lack of leadership skills under Director-General Christopher Sankolo, calling for President Joseph Boakai's immediate intervention.

a3363.speaker: Josephine George Francis, LACRA Board Chairperson and former Representative
a3363.name: Josephine George Francis
a3363.title: LACRA Board Chairperson and former Representative
a3363.speech: Cautioned employees to value their jobs and urged them to desist from unwarranted claims, only because of self-interest, but to work hard: "You know we have thousands of Youths that are unemployed, but when walking through, Red Light market, I see hundreds of Women, boys, and men selling just to survive. Even though they are in the informal sector, but they wake up every day to get ends meet, but for those of you, who have job at LACRA, you better hold it strong, because there are lot of people out there, who are competent, and willing come to LACRA."

a3497.speaker: International Crisis Group
a3497.name: International Crisis Group
a3497.speech: Says there is a high risk it will "morph into a multi-country confrontation in the Great Lakes recalling the horrors of the 1990s."

a3497.speaker: African Union (AU)
a3497.name: African Union (AU)
a3497.speech: The AU says all heads of state will attend, but it is not clear if Rwandan President Paul Kagame and his Congolese counterpart Felix Tshisekedi will meet in person.

a3497.speaker: Liesl Louw-Vaudran, International Crisis Group researcher
a3497.name: Liesl Louw-Vaudran
a3497.title: International Crisis Group researcher
a3497.speech: "The AU has the capacity to be at the forefront of peace negotiations and to put pressure on everyone to avoid a new escalation."

a3497.speaker: Joint summit of eastern and southern African blocs
a3497.name: Joint summit of eastern and southern African blocs
a3497.speech: Called for a ceasefire but failed to mention Rwanda's involvement, which is widely documented, including by the United Nations.

a3497.speaker: Benjamin Auge, researcher at France's Institute of International Relations
a3497.name: Benjamin Auge
a3497.title: researcher at France's Institute of International Relations
a3497.speech: Said it was "impossible to say who will win."

a3497.speaker: Nana Akufo-Addo, President of Ghana
a3497.name: Nana Akufo-Addo
a3497.title: President of Ghana
a3497.speech: Called in 2023 for African leaders to seek damages for the transatlantic slave trade.

a3497.speaker: Paul-Simon Handy, East Africa director at the Institute for Security Studies
a3497.name: Paul-Simon Handy
a3497.title: East Africa director at the Institute for Security Studies
a3497.speech: Said it was a bad time to broach the "divisive" issue of reparations: "It comes at a time of global geopolitics where we need consensus" between African countries and their Western partners.

a3705.speaker: Dr Abdourahmane Diallo, newly appointed Director of Programme Management at the WHO Regional Office for Africa
a3705.name: Dr Abdourahmane Diallo
a3705.title: newly appointed Director of Programme Management at the WHO Regional Office for Africa
a3705.speech: “To serve public health is to work for human dignity. I measure the responsibility of this continental mission and I carry it with humility and commitment.”

a3741.speaker: Roberta Metsola, President of the European Parliament
a3741.name: Roberta Metsola
a3741.title: President of the European Parliament
a3741.speech: “By awarding this year's Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought to Andrzej Poczobut, of Belarus, and to Mzia Amaglobeli, of Georgia, we honour two journalists whose courage shines like a beacon for all those who refuse to be silenced” ; emphasised that “both paid a high price for telling truth to power, becoming symbols of the struggle for freedom and for democracy” ; “Parliament stands by them and by all those who continue to demand freedom.”

a3741.speaker: European Parliament (statement)
a3741.name: European Parliament (statement)
a3741.speech: Recalled that the “journalist, essayist, blogger and activist of the Polish minority in Belarus” is a “well-known critic of Alexander Lukashenko's regime and author of texts on history and human rights” ; “Andrzej Poczobut has been detained many times, and has been imprisoned in a penal colony since 2021, after being sentenced to a term of eight years. Since then his health has worsened but, despite not receiving the medical care he needs, he continues to fight for freedom and for democracy. Andrzej Poczobut's current state of health is unknown and family visits are not authorised.”

a3741.speaker: European Parliament resolution of 15 March 2023
a3741.name: European Parliament resolution of 15 March 2023
a3741.speech: Called for the immediate and unconditional release of Andrzej Poczobut, considering that the accusations against him were “politically motivated” and “aimed at silencing independent voices and suppressing freedom of expression and of association.”

a3741.speaker: European Parliament (statement)
a3741.name: European Parliament (statement)
a3741.speech: On Mzia Amaglobeli: “In August she was sentenced to two years in prison on political grounds. Georgia's first political prisoner since the country's independence and a defender of freedom of expression, Mzia Amaglobeli has become the leading figure of Georgia's pro-democracy protest movement, opposing the ruling party 'Georgian Dream' since the contested elections of October 2024.”

a3741.speaker: European Parliament resolution of 19 June 2025
a3741.name: European Parliament resolution of 19 June 2025
a3741.speech: Condemned “the systemic attacks by the Georgian Dream regime on democratic institutions, the political opposition, independent media, civil society and the independence of the judiciary,” while calling for the immediate and unconditional release of Mzia Amaglobeli.

a3741.speaker: European Parliament (2024 Sakharov Prize award)
a3741.name: European Parliament (2024 Sakharov Prize award)
a3741.speech: In 2024, awarded the prize to the Venezuelan opposition figures María Corina Machado and Edmundo González Urrutia, highlighting their “courageous struggle for freedom and democracy.”

a3845.speaker: US Congressional Staff Delegation (STAFFDEL), Prime Minister Ntsokoane Matekane and UN representatives
a3845.name: US Congressional Staff Delegation (STAFFDEL)
a3845.title: Prime Minister Ntsokoane Matekane and UN representatives
a3845.speech: During meetings, discussions highlighted how US aid aligns with Lesotho's priorities: child protection, healthcare, economic reform, and food security.

a3928.speaker: Mozambican Government
a3928.name: Mozambican Government
a3928.speech: Acknowledges the impact of the suspension of United States support for various health programmes, but guarantees it has already “begun a dialogue” with that country’s representation in order to reverse or mitigate the effect of the cut; the Executive guarantees it is studying other alternatives to mitigate the situation, and appeals to the population to remain calm.

a3928.speaker: Inocêncio Impissa, Mozambican Government Spokesman
a3928.name: Inocêncio Impissa
a3928.title: Mozambican Government Spokesman
a3928.speech: “The decision taken by the United States of America (…) has an impact in Mozambique, because this funding is essential for maintaining strategic and priority programmes,” in the areas of “tuberculosis, HIV/AIDS, family planning, strengthening of the medicines supply chain, among others,” ; said the abrupt withdrawal of support “compromises, as one can imagine, in some way, the efficiency of implementation” of Health programmes and that the impact will also be reflected in the availability of human resources in the sector ; recalled that Mozambique has a ratio of 18.5 health professionals per 10,000 inhabitants, against a ratio of 45 professionals for the same population foreseen by the World Health Organization: “We are very far” from that target, and therefore “with this suspension” determined by the US it will be “a huge challenge to reach this target” ; said the suspension of US financial support to Mozambique and other African countries in the health area will have implications for the purchase and supply of essential medicines to health units, such as for HIV/AIDS and family planning.

a3928.speaker: Inocêncio Impissa, Mozambican Government Spokesman
a3928.name: Inocêncio Impissa
a3928.title: Mozambican Government Spokesman
a3928.speech: Using as an example the demonstrations in Chongoene, protesting the Government’s failure to keep promises to provide water and electricity to the Bungane community, said the protests may be the result of a lack of assistance from the megaprojects, and that a team will be formed to investigate the situation.

a3928.speaker: Inocêncio Impissa, Mozambican Government Spokesman
a3928.name: Inocêncio Impissa
a3928.title: Mozambican Government Spokesman
a3928.speech: Also advanced that payments of the thirteenth salary are already under way and that, at this moment, 50% of civil servants have been paid; the official guaranteed that the process will be concluded by Tuesday.

a4054.speaker: Sam George, Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovation
a4054.name: Sam George
a4054.title: Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovation
a4054.speech: addressed the ongoing discussions about Telecel and AT, formerly AirtelTigo. At a press briefing, the Minister clarified that the arrangement is neither a merger nor an acquisition, but rather a restructuring aimed at addressing AT's accumulated debts and strengthening the sector.

a4054.speaker: Regulators
a4054.name: Regulators
a4054.speech: have voiced concerns about this lopsided structure for years, as it risks stifling innovation and leaving consumers with fewer choices.

a4171.speaker: Michael Usi, Vice President of Malawi
a4171.name: Michael Usi
a4171.title: Vice President of Malawi
a4171.speech: Says the government, through the Department of Disaster Management Affairs (DoDMA), will continue with the Lean Season Food Insecurity Response programme to provide relief food to households that are affected by natural disasters such as drought and cyclones.

a4171.speaker: Michael Usi, Vice President of Malawi
a4171.name: Michael Usi
a4171.title: Vice President of Malawi
a4171.speech: Asked those who are charged with the responsibility to register beneficiaries to be honest when identifying and registering recipients of humanitarian assistance.

a4171.speaker: Michael Usi, Vice President of Malawi
a4171.name: Michael Usi
a4171.title: Vice President of Malawi
a4171.speech: Appealed to communities to stop cutting down trees carelessly, saying this contributes to climate change, whose effects are so devastating.

a4171.speaker: Charles Kalemba, DoDMA Commissioner
a4171.name: Charles Kalemba
a4171.title: DoDMA Commissioner
a4171.speech: Said hunger will remain, and the department will continue with Lean Season Food Insecurity Response programmes to cushion people.

a4171.speaker: Reinhard Chavula, District Commissioner for Zomba
a4171.name: Reinhard Chavula
a4171.title: District Commissioner for Zomba
a4171.speech: Hailed the government through DoDMA for responding to the situation in the district ; disclosed that 1,760 households were affected by drought while 788 households were affected by the recent Cyclone Chido in Zomba.

a4171.speaker: David Mwanyali, recipient of relief food
a4171.name: David Mwanyali
a4171.title: recipient of relief food
a4171.speech: Commended the government for responding to the plight of hunger-affected households.

a4200.speaker: Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, Chairman of NATO’s Military Committee (senior official, to Italy’s Corriere della Sera)
a4200.name: Giuseppe Cavo Dragone
a4200.title: Chairman of NATO’s Military Committee (senior official, to Italy’s Corriere della Sera)
a4200.speech: Stated that NATO has already provided more than $33 billion since January and plans to raise the total to $50 billion by the end of the year, intending to spend another $50 billion on military aid for Ukraine and match its contributions from last year.

a4200.speaker: Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, Chairman of NATO’s Military Committee
a4200.name: Giuseppe Cavo Dragone
a4200.title: Chairman of NATO’s Military Committee
a4200.speech: Asked about the alliance’s stance as Washington and Moscow pursue peace efforts, said NATO would “continue military assistance and even increase it,” accusing Russia of “stalling” dialogue; also expressed hope that Western sanctions, which he described as aimed at “increasing internal tensions” against Russian President Vladimir Putin, would be tightened.

a4200.speaker: Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, Chairman of NATO’s Military Committee
a4200.name: Giuseppe Cavo Dragone
a4200.title: Chairman of NATO’s Military Committee
a4200.speech: Dismissed speculation that NATO could deploy troops to Ukraine, stressing that “we have not spoken about this at all in NATO, we have not even mentioned it,” adding that such proposals were “at least premature” and remained “in their infancy.”
