a4200.speaker: The White House
a4200.name: The White House
a4200.speech: Said there was “light at the end of the tunnel.”

a4200.speaker: Moscow / Russian officials
a4200.name: Moscow / Russian officials
a4200.speech: Moscow has indicated it is open to negotiations and has welcomed Trump’s efforts to resolve the conflict by addressing its root causes; Russia has repeatedly condemned NATO arms deliveries, arguing they only prolong the conflict; officials in Moscow have questioned whether Kiev and its European backers are genuinely committed to peace, pointing out that Zelensky has rejected most of Trump’s proposals and continues to insist on reclaiming Crimea and other former Ukrainian territories; Moscow has also criticized European NATO members for trying to sideline Russia in the negotiations while focusing instead on security guarantees for Kiev, which Russia has branded an illegitimate and “openly neo-Nazi” regime.

a4211.speaker: Willard, acting District Development Coordinator of Gokwe North
a4211.name: Willard
a4211.title: acting District Development Coordinator of Gokwe North
a4211.speech: Urged the residents to prioritise handwashing as a crucial step in safeguarding public health ; expressed gratitude to the organisers for choosing a dip tank as the venue, a decision resonating with the mantra of “leaving no one and no place behind.”

a4211.speaker: Dzingirai Beauty, Africa Ahead representative
a4211.name: Dzingirai Beauty
a4211.title: Africa Ahead representative
a4211.speech: Acknowledged the support of the government in facilitating community development projects funded by USAID and highlighted ongoing initiatives such as the installation of piped water schemes and the construction of dip tanks: “Our projects are aimed at improving the lives of people in communities, with a primary focus on enhancing sanitation.”

a4211.speaker: Representative of the Rural Infrastructure Development Agency (RIDA) (anonymous)
a4211.name: Representative of the Rural Infrastructure Development Agency (RIDA) (anonymous)
a4211.speech: Commended Africa Ahead for their dedication to promoting hand hygiene in rural communities ; added that handwashing is essential in bringing sanity to the communities as they will have access to clean water and they will embark on various sanitation projects.

a4211.speaker: Christopher Mandima, Gokwe North District Environmental Health Officer
a4211.name: Christopher Mandima
a4211.title: Gokwe North District Environmental Health Officer
a4211.speech: Underscored the importance of hand hygiene, offering practical advice for those lacking soap or detergents, suggesting the use of ash as an alternative.

a4236.speaker: Helen Khungwa Chira, USAID Zambia nutrition advisor
a4236.name: Helen Khungwa Chira
a4236.title: USAID Zambia nutrition advisor
a4236.speech: Says the Bicycle Innovation Programme (BIP) aims to tackle development challenges in sub-Saharan Africa through the increased adoption of bicycles: “The BIP aims to achieve this by incentivising the development and scaling of innovative solutions relating to bicycles within an open innovation programme structure” ; said USAID’s country development cooperation strategy in Malawi and Zambia has a specific focus on reducing rural poverty through enterprise-driven economic growth.

a4318.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a4318.name: Donald Trump
a4318.title: President of the United States
a4318.speech: Recently stated that he was halting foreign aid from the US to many countries, some of which are in Africa.

a4318.speaker: African Development Bank (report)
a4318.name: African Development Bank (report)
a4318.speech: According to a report published by the African Development Bank, Africa lost around US$2 trillion between 1970 and 2018 due to capital flight, which is well above the continent’s external debt.

a4467.speaker: Shakira, singer
a4467.name: Shakira
a4467.title: singer
a4467.speech: “I’ve worked for over a year, polishing every single detail of the show, so this is really an amazing reward” ; “I came here for the Beyoncé concert and that was flawless, so you’d better make me sound like that” ; “I warn you, I might not make a lot of sense right now. I’m still recovering. It was really hot today and humid. So whenever it’s like that, or there’s altitude, it’s very challenging… but totally worth it.” ; “To put together a show of this size, and to make it happen every night, it doesn’t matter if you’re sad or if you had a bad day or if you’re sick or you’re coughing – you just have to do your best and miraculously make it happen. And the adrenalin actually doesn’t let me feel the exhaustion, or how demanding it can be. It carries you through.”

a4467.speaker: Shakira, singer
a4467.name: Shakira
a4467.title: singer
a4467.speech: Said on stage: “Many of you know that the past years haven’t been the easiest for me. But who doesn’t have a fall here and there, right? What I’ve learned is that a fall isn’t the end, but the beginning of an even better journey.”

a4467.speaker: Shakira, singer
a4467.name: Shakira
a4467.title: singer
a4467.speech: “I was only 19 when I moved to the US, like many other Colombian immigrants who come to this country looking for a better future” ; “And I remember I was surrounded by Spanish-English dictionaries and synonym dictionaries – because back in the day I didn’t really have Google or ChatGPT to [help]. So it was all very precarious. And then I got into poetry and started reading a little bit of a Leonard Cohen and Walt Whitman and Bob Dylan, trying to understand how the English language works within songwriting. I think that’s how I got good at it.”

a4467.speaker: Shakira, singer
a4467.name: Shakira
a4467.title: singer
a4467.speech: Accepting the Grammy for best Latin pop album: “I want to dedicate this award to all my immigrant brothers and sisters in this country. You are loved, you are worth it, and I will always fight with you.” ; on being an immigrant in the US today: “It means living in constant fear. And it’s painful to see. Now, more than ever, we have to remain united. Now, more than ever, we have to raise our voices and make it very clear that a country can change its immigration policies, but the treatment of all people must always be humane.”

a4467.speaker: Shakira, singer
a4467.name: Shakira
a4467.title: singer
a4467.speech: On her children appearing on the video screens during Acróstico: “My heart melts every time I see them on that screen and I hear their little voices” ; “They’re just everything to me. They’re my engine and the reason why I’m alive. So having them every night on stage, it’s just such a precious moment.”

a4467.speaker: Hannah Kinkade, head of wardrobe
a4467.name: Hannah Kinkade
a4467.title: head of wardrobe
a4467.speech: “We travel with two washing machines and two tumble dryers, which we plumb in [at] every venue” ; said every outfit has to be refreshed before a new show because “Shakira dances really hard and the dancers do as well. The male dancers scuff their shoes so badly that we have to repaint them every morning.”

a4467.speaker: Kevin Rowe, stage manager
a4467.name: Kevin Rowe
a4467.title: stage manager
a4467.speech: On working on an outdoor show: “It either gets very hot or very wet. But that’s the trade-off of living in the underworld.”

a4467.speaker: Darina Littleton, chief dancer
a4467.name: Darina Littleton
a4467.title: chief dancer
a4467.speech: “When she’s on, she’s on. When she comes in, she’s ready, her character’s on, she’s full out.”

a4467.speaker: Tim Mitchell, musical director
a4467.name: Tim Mitchell
a4467.title: musical director
a4467.speech: “She knows what she wants, and if she can’t figure it out she’ll get there one way or another” ; “She’s very particular about every aspect of the show: Sound, visual, lighting, the wristbands, every single thing. It’s incredible. I don’t know how she does it.”

a4467.speaker: A fan (unnamed), attending the Miami show
a4467.name: A fan (unnamed)
a4467.title: attending the Miami show
a4467.speech: “She’s so inspiring to women. She’s done it all. She is power.”

a4505.speaker: World Bank
a4505.name: World Bank
a4505.speech: Has projected a growth rate of 3.5% for Africa, despite global economic uncertainty.

a4505.speaker: Tony Elumelu, Nigerian Economist
a4505.name: Tony Elumelu
a4505.title: Nigerian Economist
a4505.speech: "We have to take responsibility for our own development. No one else will develop Africa for us."

a4505.speaker: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf, former Liberian President
a4505.name: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf
a4505.title: former Liberian President
a4505.speech: "The future of Africa lies in the hands of its people."

a4505.speaker: African Union member state leaders (38th AU Summit, February 2025)
a4505.name: African Union member state leaders (38th AU Summit
a4505.title: February 2025)
a4505.speech: Agreed on this year's theme for Africa Day during the 38th AU Summit held in February 2025, with the objective of placing reparations at the core of the AU's long-term priorities and strengthening its capacity to provide technical support to member states in this endeavour.

a4570.speaker: US Central Command for the Middle East (Centcom) (statement)
a4570.name: US Central Command for the Middle East (Centcom) (statement)
a4570.speech: Reported in a statement that "Initial analyses indicate that one of the crew members was slightly injured." ; According to Centcom, the guided-missile cruiser USS Gettysburg "fired by mistake (...) and hit" an F/A-18 combat aircraft carrying the two US Navy pilots who had taken off from the aircraft carrier USS Harry S. Truman.

a4570.speaker: US military
a4570.name: US military
a4570.speech: Stated that "The incident was not the result of hostile fire," and that an investigation has been opened into "a suspected case of friendly fire."

a4570.speaker: Houthi rebels
a4570.name: Houthi rebels
a4570.speech: Say they are acting in solidarity with the Palestinians in the context of the war in the Gaza Strip between Israel and Hamas ; claimed the strike that caused 16 light injuries in central Israel.

a4570.speaker: United States
a4570.name: United States
a4570.speech: Said on Saturday that it had destroyed Houthi military installations in the Yemeni capital, Sanaa.

a4570.speaker: US Central Command for the Middle East (Centcom)
a4570.name: US Central Command for the Middle East (Centcom)
a4570.speech: According to Centcom, rebel drones and cruise missiles were also shot down over the Red Sea.

a4693.speaker: Guled Ahmed, author of ‘Al-Shabaab Mafia Inc.’, Non-Resident Scholar at the Middle East Institute
a4693.name: Guled Ahmed
a4693.title: author of ‘Al-Shabaab Mafia Inc.’, Non-Resident Scholar at the Middle East Institute
a4693.speech: Argues that the dominant narratives, often shaped by institutions and individuals without deep psychological or grassroots understanding, have consistently failed to capture the group’s true dynamics ; challenges years of global agency reports and Western analyses that only skim the surface, citing the frequently repeated estimate that Al-Shabaab generates 120 million US dollars annually, a figure that has barely changed in over a decade of reports and that ignores both inflation and Somalia’s expanding economy, concealing the group’s actual financial reach, which the author argues may now be closer to one billion dollars a year.

a4693.speaker: Al-Shabaab
a4693.name: Al-Shabaab
a4693.speech: Has publicly sworn to burn copies of the book inside Somalia, issuing threats against its circulation.

a4762.speaker: India (Government of India) / India’s foreign ministry (statement)
a4762.name: India (Government of India) / India’s foreign ministry (statement)
a4762.speech: Has called Donald Trump’s threat of “substantially” higher tariffs over its purchase of oil from Russia “unjustified and unreasonable” ; “Like any major economy, India will take all necessary measures to safeguard its national interests and economic security” ; “The targeting of India is unjustified and unreasonable” ; also criticised the US – its largest trading partner – for introducing the tariffs when the US itself is still doing trade with Russia.

a4762.speaker: Randhir Jaiswal, spokesperson for India’s foreign ministry
a4762.name: Randhir Jaiswal
a4762.title: spokesperson for India’s foreign ministry
a4762.speech: Said the US had encouraged India to import Russian gas at the start of the conflict, “for strengthening global energy markets stability” ; said India “began importing from Russia because traditional supplies were diverted to Europe after the outbreak of the conflict.”

a4762.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (post on Truth Social)
a4762.name: Donald Trump
a4762.title: US President (post on Truth Social)
a4762.speech: Warned he would raise levies, saying India “don’t care how many people in Ukraine are being killed by the Russian War Machine” ; “India is not only buying massive amounts of Russian Oil, they are then, for much of the Oil purchased, selling it on the Open Market for big profits” ; “Because of this, I will be substantially raising the Tariff paid by India to the USA.”

a4762.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4762.name: Donald Trump
a4762.title: US President
a4762.speech: Last week had described India as a “friend” but said its tariffs on US products “are far too high” and he warned of an unspecified “penalty” over its trade with Russia.

a4762.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4762.name: Donald Trump
a4762.title: US President
a4762.speech: Has questioned whether Putin is truly committed to peace with Ukraine; in Monday’s Truth Social post he used stern language, describing the Russian military as the “Russian War Machine” ; has threatened Moscow with severe tariffs targeting its oil and other exports if a ceasefire with Ukraine is not agreed by 8 August.

a4762.speaker: Bloomberg (citing people familiar with the situation)
a4762.name: Bloomberg (citing people familiar with the situation)
a4762.speech: Reported that Prime Minister Narendra Modi has not ordered India’s oil refineries to stop buying Russian oil.

a4762.speaker: Ajay Srivastava, former Indian trade official and head of the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI)
a4762.name: Ajay Srivastava
a4762.title: former Indian trade official and head of the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI)
a4762.speech: Said Trump’s claims about India’s oil trade with Russia are misleading for several reasons ; told the BBC that the trade has been transparent and broadly understood by the US ; said India ramped up purchases of oil to help stabilise global markets after Western sanctions disrupted supplies – helping to stop a global oil price shock ; also said that India’s oil refineries – both public and private – decide where to buy crude oil based on factors like price, supply security, and export rules, and that they operate independently of the government and do not need its approval to buy from Russia or other countries.

a4762.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President
a4762.name: Vladimir Putin
a4762.title: Russian President
a4762.speech: Has repeatedly said he is ready for peace but only if Kyiv meets certain conditions, such as recognising Ukrainian territories that Russia has occupied.

a4825.speaker: Amour Allossoukpo, officer in charge of visits at the Songhai Centre
a4825.name: Amour Allossoukpo
a4825.title: officer in charge of visits at the Songhai Centre
a4825.speech: describes the integrated recycling circuits: "Waste from crop production is used for animal production. Animal droppings go into making the compost that is used to fertilise the soil. Waste from crop production is used for fish farming, just as the water from fish farming can be used to water the gardens or give the animals something to drink. The droppings are used to produce maggots to feed the fish" ; "Waste from crop production, the droppings and the water from fish farming are used to produce the bioenergy we call biogas"

a4825.speaker: Amour Allossoukpo, officer in charge of visits at the Songhai Centre
a4825.name: Amour Allossoukpo
a4825.title: officer in charge of visits at the Songhai Centre
a4825.speech: explains how compost is made: "To make the compost we use animal droppings and anything that can decompose. Once the heap is made, it must be watered abundantly and mulched so that the sun's rays do not destroy the micro-organisms that are supposed to speed up decomposition"

a4825.speaker: Amour Allossoukpo, officer in charge of visits at the Songhai Centre (the guide)
a4825.name: Amour Allossoukpo
a4825.title: officer in charge of visits at the Songhai Centre (the guide)
a4825.speech: adds, on the irrigation system: "There, as you can see, they are installing a drip system"

a4825.speaker: Amour Allossoukpo, officer in charge of visits at the Songhai Centre
a4825.name: Amour Allossoukpo
a4825.title: officer in charge of visits at the Songhai Centre
a4825.speech: justifies raising the animals on stilts: "Under these stilts we put straw, onto which the droppings fall directly, and we collect them to make the compost used to fertilise the soil"

a4825.speaker: Amour Allossoukpo, officer in charge of visits at the Songhai Centre
a4825.name: Amour Allossoukpo
a4825.title: officer in charge of visits at the Songhai Centre
a4825.speech: details the water and fish-farming circuit: "Often, when it arrives, the water takes on a red colour. We put the chickens' droppings into the water, which fertilises the water ... So, after three weeks, the water gradually turns green again. That means it is producing algae. The fish feed on these algae" ; "These hyacinths make it possible to purify the dirty water coming from the processing units and the kitchen. In return, these hyacinths are mixed with pig droppings to be used to produce the biogas" ; "These breeding tilapias lay eggs and, after hatching, release the fry from their mouths. To feed them we give them pellets, sweet potato leaves or maggots recovered from the liquid manure of the laying hens"

a4825.speaker: Godfrey Nzamujo, founder of the Songhai Centre and former engineering professor in the United States
a4825.name: Godfrey Nzamujo
a4825.title: founder of the Songhai Centre and former engineering professor in the United States
a4825.speech: recalls why he returned to Africa: "I decided to go back to Africa to change ways of doing things according to a new vision of the world. I understood that you have to learn to dance with nature so that it opens itself to us. So, instead of giving lectures here and there, I set to work here" ; "I took this land that had been exhausted by chemicals. On that side not even weeds would grow any more. The soil was dead" ; "Today we produce all year round, three times more than conventional farming and of exceptional quality. This site has become a book in which everyone can read. It is proof that if you connect with nature, it responds. It is called biomimicry. You have to create a framework in which you let the systems work in synergy"

a4825.speaker: One of the Nigerian nuns of the congregation of the Little Sisters of the Poor visiting the centre
a4825.name: One of the Nigerian nuns of the congregation of the Little Sisters of the Poor visiting the centre
a4825.speech: confesses: "You realise that everything is possible"

a4825.speaker: Justin Lekoto, one of the department heads at the Songhai Centre
a4825.name: Justin Lekoto
a4825.title: one of the department heads at the Songhai Centre
a4825.speech: stresses: "It is so that we can cover all the agro-ecological zones of Benin, be closer to the people. In this way this model, based on ecology, with integrated and diversified agricultural production, and which constitutes a solution for Africa to escape poverty, can be adopted by all the communities that wish to do so. We exploit the potential of the zone in which we are established to develop production"

a4935.speaker: Leevi Katoma, Swapo Party MP
a4935.name: Leevi Katoma
a4935.title: Swapo Party MP
a4935.speech: moved a motion expressing unwavering solidarity with Cuba, highlighting the historical ties between Namibia and Cuba.

a4935.speaker: Henny Seibeb, Landless People's Movement MP
a4935.name: Henny Seibeb
a4935.title: Landless People's Movement MP
a4935.speech: presented a motion emphasising solidarity with Palestine amidst the escalating conflict in the Gaza Strip, calling for adherence to international law, an immediate ceasefire, and support for a two-state solution.

a4935.speaker: Patience Masua, Swapo MP
a4935.name: Patience Masua
a4935.title: Swapo MP
a4935.speech: introduced a motion asserting Namibia's support for the urgent decolonisation of Western Sahara and the Saharawi people's right to self-determination, condemning Morocco's illegal occupation, and calling for a free and fair referendum under UN supervision.

a5380.speaker: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a5380.name: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a5380.speech: says that since then, the number of children in desperate need of assistance in Nigeria has doubled.

a5380.speaker: Yagana Bulama, Nigerian mother of twins
a5380.name: Yagana Bulama
a5380.title: Nigerian mother of twins
a5380.speech: said she has been entirely dependent on humanitarian aid ; “Unfortunately, both were diagnosed with malnutrition by the Mercy Corps Nutrition team and were enrolled in their Outpatient Therapeutic Program at Fulatari,” she said ; “As a result of the interruption in their care, my twins’ health deteriorated. Tragically, I lost one of them.”

a5380.speaker: Trond Jensen, head of OCHA’s office in Nigeria
a5380.name: Trond Jensen
a5380.title: head of OCHA’s office in Nigeria
a5380.speech: said the situation is dire. “What we are seeing is that 50 per cent of the nutrition efforts that we have put in place are now gone. And 70 per cent of health support is under threat, if it hasn’t disappeared already.” ; said the organisation’s capacity to deal with it “has halved or even worse” ; says immediate support is needed if they are to have any hope of saving the children.

a5474.speaker: Syrian government
a5474.name: Syrian government
a5474.speech: Announced that Bedouin fighters have been cleared from the city of Suwayda and that government forces have been deployed to oversee their exit from the entire governorate.

a5474.speaker: Ahmed al-Sharaa, Syrian President
a5474.name: Ahmed al-Sharaa
a5474.title: Syrian President
a5474.speech: Ordered a new ceasefire between Bedouin and Druze groups ; in a televised statement on Saturday, called on all parties to lay down arms and help the government restore peace: "While we thank the [Bedouin] clans for their heroic stance, we call on them to adhere to the ceasefire and follow the orders of the state." "All should understand this moment requires unity and full cooperation, so we can overcome these challenges and preserve our country from foreign interference and internal sedition."

a5474.speaker: Ahmed al-Sharaa, Syrian President
a5474.name: Ahmed al-Sharaa
a5474.title: Syrian President
a5474.speech: Condemned Israel's attacks, saying it "pushed the country into a dangerous phase that threatened its stability."

a5474.speaker: Nour al-Din Baba, spokesman for the Syrian Ministry of Interior
a5474.name: Nour al-Din Baba
a5474.title: spokesman for the Syrian Ministry of Interior
a5474.speech: Said in a statement carried by the official Sana news agency that the fighting ended "following intensive efforts" to implement the ceasefire agreement and the deployment of government forces in the northern and western areas of Suwayda province. He said the city of Suwayda has now been "cleared of all tribal fighters, and clashes within the city's neighbourhoods have been brought to a halt."

a5474.speaker: Syrian Ministry of Health
a5474.name: Syrian Ministry of Health
a5474.speech: At least 260 people have been killed in the fighting, and 1,700 others have been wounded, according to the Syrian Ministry of Health.

a5474.speaker: Bedouin factions (statement)
a5474.name: Bedouin factions (statement)
a5474.speech: "Following consultations with all members of Suwayda's clans and tribes, we have decided to adhere to the ceasefire, prioritise reason and restraint, and allow the state's authorised institutions the space to carry out their responsibilities in restoring security and stability." ; "Therefore, we declare that all our fighters have been withdrawn from the city of Suwayda."

a5474.speaker: Mohamed Vall, Al Jazeera correspondent reporting from Damascus
a5474.name: Mohamed Vall
a5474.title: Al Jazeera correspondent reporting from Damascus
a5474.speech: Said the Druze, too, seemed to have accepted the truce: "Hikmat Al Hajri, a prominent spiritual leader, has called for all Bedouin fighters to be escorted safely out of Suwayda." "Security forces from the interior ministry have been deployed to help separate rival groups, and oversee the implementation of the ceasefire. But there are still reports of ongoing fighting in the city, with some Druze leaders voicing strong opposition to the cessation of hostilities." "So while there is hope, there is also doubt that this conflict is over."

a5474.speaker: Hikmat Al Hajri, prominent Druze spiritual leader
a5474.name: Hikmat Al Hajri
a5474.title: prominent Druze spiritual leader
a5474.speech: Has called for all Bedouin fighters to be escorted safely out of Suwayda.

a5474.speaker: Jordanian government (readout)
a5474.name: Jordanian government (readout)
a5474.speech: Jordanian Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi, his Syrian counterpart Asaad al-Shibani and the US special envoy for Syria, Thomas Barak, "discussed the situation in Syria and efforts to consolidate the ceasefire reached around Suwayda Governorate to prevent bloodshed and preserve the safety of civilians", according to a readout by the Jordanian government. The three officials agreed on "practical steps" to support the ceasefire, including the release of detainees held by all parties, Syrian security force deployments and community reconciliation efforts.

a5474.speaker: Ayman Safadi, Jordanian Foreign Minister
a5474.name: Ayman Safadi
a5474.title: Jordanian Foreign Minister
a5474.speech: Welcomed the Syrian government's "commitment to holding accountable all those responsible for violations against Syrian citizens" in the Suwayda area.

a5474.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State (post on X)
a5474.name: Marco Rubio
a5474.title: US Secretary of State (post on X)
a5474.speech: Urged Syrian government troops to prevent fighters from entering Suwayda and "carrying out massacres": "They must hold accountable and bring to justice anyone guilty of atrocities including those in their own ranks. Furthermore the fighting between Druze and Bedouin groups inside the perimeter must also stop immediately."

a5474.speaker: David Lammy, United Kingdom foreign secretary (post on X)
a5474.name: David Lammy
a5474.title: United Kingdom foreign secretary (post on X)
a5474.speech: Said he was horrified by the violence in southern Syria and that "a sustainable ceasefire is vital".

a5474.speaker: France's Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs
a5474.name: France's Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs
a5474.speech: Stressed the need for "Syrian authorities to ensure the safety and rights of all segments of the Syrian people", and called for investigations into abuses against civilians in Suwayda.

a5474.speaker: Japan (government)
a5474.name: Japan (government)
a5474.speech: Expressed concern over the violence, including the Israeli strikes, and called for the ceasefire to be implemented swiftly. It added that it "strongly urges all parties concerned to exercise maximum restraint, preserve Syria's territorial integrity and national unity, and respect its independence and sovereignty".

a5536.speaker: Fortune (business magazine)
a5536.name: Fortune (business magazine)
a5536.speech: Named Enron ‘America’s Most Innovative Company’ for six consecutive years.

a5536.speaker: Charles Hugh Smith (writer)
a5536.name: Charles Hugh Smith (writer)
a5536.speech: Coined/used the term the ‘permanent government’, cited for the idea that healthy competitors are weeded out to suit its desires.

a5536.speaker: Amanda Hocking, author of Hollowland
a5536.name: Amanda Hocking
a5536.title: author of Hollowland
a5536.speech: “This is the way the world ends; not with a bang or a whimper, but with zombies breaking down the back door.”

a5661.speaker: The Quran (Coran 2/183, 27/88, 41/53)
a5661.name: The Quran (Coran 2/183
a5661.speech: “O you who believe! Fasting has been prescribed for you as it was prescribed for those before you, so that you may attain piety” (Quran 2/183) ; “Such is the work of Allah, who has perfected all things. He is Fully Aware of what you do!” (Quran 27/88) ; “We will show them Our signs in the universe and within themselves, until it becomes clear to them that this (the Quran) is the truth. Is it not enough that your Lord is witness over all things?” (Quran 41/53)

a5661.speaker: Doctors (physicians generally)
a5661.name: Doctors (physicians generally)
a5661.speech: Have spoken at length about the benefits of fasting; said, among other things, that it rids the stomach and intestines of toxic residues remaining in the body and relieves the digestive system; affirm that fasting is useful for treating countless illnesses such as obesity, because it helps to lose weight quickly and by simple means.

a5661.speaker: Dr. Muhammad Abû Chawk, in an article entitled “Fasting and the nervous system”
a5661.name: Dr. Muhammad Abû Chawk
a5661.title: in an article entitled “Fasting and the nervous system”
a5661.speech: Affirms that: “The spirituality of fasting gives rise to a purification and an education of the soul, just as it gives rise to endurance and compassion towards the poor and the needy. It spares the servant from sinking into pleasures with their unfortunate consequences, it purifies the soul by cultivating noble virtues such as sincerity, probity, distance from anger, vengeance, hatred, envy and rancour. This spirituality confers on the human soul a spirit of peace, affection and sincerity, which in turn is reflected in the nervous system, whose rest calms the other organs of the body and whose irritation irritates the other organs. In fact, when the nervous system revolts, the other organs, whose role is to safeguard the strength of the body, also revolt. What a divine moral! To make the fasting person an ‘angel’ in the form of a man, so that he may enjoy his life and delight others” ; and adds: “I say to those who consult psychiatrists in search of a remedy for nervous tension, anxiety, insomnia and depression, and other nervous illnesses: here is the month of Ramadan. If you hold fast to its spirituality and the good it confers on you, you will never need remedies or medicines.”

a5661.speaker: A non-Muslim doctor
a5661.name: A non-Muslim doctor
a5661.speech: Indicated: “Fasting, for a single month in the year, allows the body to eliminate the putrefied food residues of a whole year.”

a5661.speaker: Macfadden, American scholar, pioneer of physical culture in the United States and specialist in hygiene
a5661.name: Macfadden
a5661.title: American scholar, pioneer of physical culture in the United States and specialist in hygiene
a5661.speech: Affirmed, as did other specialists, that “fasting is useful for the body, because it cleanses it of the toxic residues coming from certain foods and medicines”; he affirms he succeeded in treating most illnesses with fasting, noting that the benefit patients derive varies according to the severity of the illness, and that fasting is most effective against gastric illnesses: “Fasting accelerates in an extraordinary way the healing of gastric illnesses, followed by blood diseases, then bone diseases, such as rheumatism” ; “Every human being, especially a sick one, needs to fast. In fact, foods and medicines accumulate in his body and give him the appearance of a sick person, because they weigh him down and reduce his activity. As soon as he fasts, these toxic substances break down and disappear until his body becomes completely pure” ; he recommended that everyone fast, repeating his famous maxim: “Fasting is the remedy for every incurable illness.”

a5661.speaker: Dr. Robert Barthlow, American physician
a5661.name: Dr. Robert Barthlow
a5661.title: American physician
a5661.speech: Affirms: “Indeed, fasting is an effective means of getting rid of all sorts of microbes, including syphilis, because it destroys the cells, then rebuilds them. That is the foundation of the starvation theory for treating syphilis.”

a5736.speaker: Save the Children (NGO)
a5736.name: Save the Children (NGO)
a5736.speech: Warns that several Sudanese children are in peril in the face of the exhaustion of resources around the Zamzam refugee camp; warns of an imminent catastrophe and states that its mobile health clinics have only two days' worth of medical supplies left; according to the NGO, the destruction of the camp's main market has further worsened food insecurity, pushing inhabitants to extreme measures such as consuming animal feed; says it has stocks of medicines and medical equipment in a warehouse in Tawila, 60 km from Zamzam, but insecurity and road closures prevent their delivery; calls on the international community to act urgently to guarantee safe humanitarian access and the unhindered delivery of food and medical aid; and says it continues to provide vital support to children and their families, having been present in Sudan since 1983.

a5736.speaker: Mohamed Abdiladif, Save the Children country director for Sudan
a5736.name: Mohamed Abdiladif
a5736.title: Save the Children country director for Sudan
a5736.speech: “For several months now, our staff have been seeing visible signs of severe malnutrition and serious illness among children.” ; “Our efforts are continually hampered by stock-outs of essential medicines and therapeutic foods.” ; “Children are always the first victims of famine and disease. Without immediate intervention, we are going to witness an avoidable slaughter.”

a5736.speaker: World Health Organization
a5736.name: World Health Organization
a5736.speech: According to the World Health Organization, more than 30 million people will need aid in 2025, including 16 million children.

a5817.speaker: Abigail Kadirire, 42-year-old single mother-of-six farmer, Kamutepe village, Rushinga
a5817.name: Abigail Kadirire
a5817.title: 42-year-old single mother-of-six farmer, Kamutepe village, Rushinga
a5817.speech: "This is the second time this farming season that I am seeing it in my fields," she said ; "I sowed again in early January 2025 after struggling to get the seeds. Then fall armyworm came and ravaged my maize crops," she said ; "I thought this year I was going to have a good harvest, but it is now uncertain because of the pests."

a5817.speaker: Abigail Kadirire, 42-year-old single mother-of-six farmer, Kamutepe village, Rushinga
a5817.name: Abigail Kadirire
a5817.title: 42-year-old single mother-of-six farmer, Kamutepe village, Rushinga
a5817.speech: "It is not easy to survive on handouts. But after the fall armyworm decreased yields on my maize crop this year, it appears I will survive on handouts again," Kadirire said.

a5817.speaker: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
a5817.name: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
a5817.speech: According to the FAO, the armyworm, native to the Americas, was first detected in central and western Africa in early 2016, and within two years had spread across almost all of sub-Saharan Africa.

a5817.speaker: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
a5817.name: United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO)
a5817.speech: According to FAO, fall armyworm reduces maize yields by up to 73% and inflicts annual economic losses valued at $9.4 billion in Africa alone.

a5817.speaker: Patrice Talla, subregional coordinator for Southern Africa at the FAO and FAO representative in Eswatini, Lesotho and Zimbabwe
a5817.name: Patrice Talla
a5817.title: subregional coordinator for Southern Africa at the FAO and FAO representative in Eswatini, Lesotho and Zimbabwe
a5817.speech: "Climate change has contributed to outbreaks of migratory pests beyond their regions of origin, notably the fall armyworm," said Talla ; said more erratic rainfall and rising temperatures have created favourable conditions for the proliferation of various pests in Zimbabwe and throughout Africa ; "Global climate warming triggers an expansion of insect geographic coverage, increasing overwintering survival and the number of generations."

a5817.speaker: Patrice Talla, subregional coordinator for Southern Africa at the FAO
a5817.name: Patrice Talla
a5817.title: subregional coordinator for Southern Africa at the FAO
a5817.speech: "Reduced (maize) harvests result in lower incomes for affected households, compromising their capacity to buy food and other necessities," Talla said.

a5817.speaker: Patrice Talla, subregional coordinator for Southern Africa at the FAO
a5817.name: Patrice Talla
a5817.title: subregional coordinator for Southern Africa at the FAO
a5817.speech: Said farmers could also use the Fall Armyworm Monitoring and Early Warning System (FAMEWS), a mobile app developed by the FAO to record data on fall armyworm through pheromone trap checks and field scouting.

a5817.speaker: Simbarashe Nyamasoka, acting deputy director, Migratory Pests Control Department, Ministry of Lands (Zimbabwe)
a5817.name: Simbarashe Nyamasoka
a5817.title: acting deputy director, Migratory Pests Control Department, Ministry of Lands (Zimbabwe)
a5817.speech: Said climate change has led to the prevalence of warm temperatures and wet conditions, allowing pests to expand their geographical range ; "Climate change has altered migratory patterns, allowing the armyworm to invade new areas more easily, potentially affecting agricultural regions that were previously less affected," Nyamasoka told Thomson Reuters Foundation/Context.

a5817.speaker: Simbarashe Nyamasoka, acting deputy director, Migratory Pests Control Department, Ministry of Lands (Zimbabwe)
a5817.name: Simbarashe Nyamasoka
a5817.title: acting deputy director, Migratory Pests Control Department, Ministry of Lands (Zimbabwe)
a5817.speech: Said climate-resilient agriculture, integrated pest management and regenerative agriculture are vital ; "Adopting climate-smart agricultural practices such as drought-resistant crops, intercropping, and organic composting, promoting practices that enhance soil health and biodiversity... and combining biological, cultural, mechanical, and chemical methods helps manage the pests sustainably," Nyamasoka said.

a5817.speaker: Simon Manguri, farmer from Kaidza village, Rushinga
a5817.name: Simon Manguri
a5817.title: farmer from Kaidza village, Rushinga
a5817.speech: Said his harvest this year would only be half of what he expected after fall armyworm infested his fields in January ; "Farming is my only source of income. I sell surplus to the government earning money to feed, clothe and send my children to school," said the father-of-five.

a5817.speaker: Dr. Christian Thierfelder, principal cropping systems agronomist at CIMMYT
a5817.name: Dr. Christian Thierfelder
a5817.title: principal cropping systems agronomist at CIMMYT
a5817.speech: Said the environmental effect of pesticides was also a consideration so farmers were also exploring traditional practices like intercropping and multiple cropping ; "And also the use of methods and practices ... like push-pull systems where you have legumes integrated with maize that repel fall armyworm," he said.

a5817.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5817.name: Donald Trump
a5817.title: US President
a5817.speech: Announced a 90-day freeze on foreign aid in January.

a5854.speaker: Siza Mzimela, CEO of Transnet Freight Rail
a5854.name: Siza Mzimela
a5854.title: CEO of Transnet Freight Rail
a5854.speech: Sent a letter to staff on Thursday reminding them of the progress made in the past three years, thanking them for their service, and urging them to not give up the fight to make TFR a success.

a5854.speaker: Siza Mzimela, CEO of Transnet Freight Rail
a5854.name: Siza Mzimela
a5854.title: CEO of Transnet Freight Rail
a5854.speech: In her letter to TFR employees, highlighted the difficulties that TFR has faced in accessing spare parts for the Chinese locomotives, resulting in a train shortage.

a5854.speaker: Siza Mzimela, CEO of Transnet Freight Rail
a5854.name: Siza Mzimela
a5854.title: CEO of Transnet Freight Rail
a5854.speech: Noted among the achievements during her tenure the introduction of borderless trains with Mozambique, the introduction of additional junior miners into the manganese sector, a new manganese export line to East London, and the repair of the container corridor after it was damaged by floods.

a5854.speaker: Pravin Gordhan, Minister of Public Enterprises
a5854.name: Pravin Gordhan
a5854.title: Minister of Public Enterprises
a5854.speech: Earlier this week described Mzimela as "relatively new to the rail sector" and said that there were skilled and experienced people who could do the job that he had learned about in "the recent past."

a5854.speaker: Minerals Council
a5854.name: Minerals Council
a5854.speech: Estimated that SA companies forfeited R100 billion in revenue, which would have netted between R40 billion to R50 billion in tax revenues for the state.

a5869.speaker: Minister of Commerce of Niger (order of 21 November 2024)
a5869.name: Minister of Commerce of Niger (order of 21 November 2024)
a5869.speech: By an order issued on 21 November 2024, banned the export of scrap metal; the order specifies that "scrap metal is understood to mean debris of iron, cast-iron or steel parts, and metal parts that are out of use."

a5869.speaker: Ministry of Commerce and Industry of Niger
a5869.name: Ministry of Commerce and Industry of Niger
a5869.speech: Announces that "the export of other categories of metals (aluminium, copper, lead, etc.) is subject to prior authorisation from the Ministry of Commerce and Industry" ; warns that "sworn agents of the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, customs agents, and the other defence and security forces are empowered to record and punish infringements of the provisions of the present order in accordance with the texts in force" ; has also banned the export of cement 32.

a5892.speaker: Tunisia (Ministry of Foreign Affairs statement)
a5892.name: Tunisia (Ministry of Foreign Affairs statement)
a5892.speech: Welcomed on Saturday the advisory opinion handed down by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) on Israel’s obligations in the occupied Palestinian territory, describing it as a “historic step” in the legal recognition of Palestinian rights ; stressed that the ICJ opinion confirms “the illegitimacy of the presence of the occupying Zionist entity” and its “total absence of any sovereign right” over the Palestinian territories ; recalled that Tunisia actively took part in the advisory proceedings through a written memorandum and oral pleadings in support of the Palestinian people’s right to self-determination and to international assistance.

a5892.speaker: Tunisia (Ministry of Foreign Affairs statement)
a5892.name: Tunisia (Ministry of Foreign Affairs statement)
a5892.speech: Considering that these obligations highlight the flagrant violations committed by the occupying entity against international humanitarian law, human rights and the United Nations Charter, Tunisia strongly urged all member states to exert pressure on the illegitimate usurping entity so that it complies with the ICJ opinion, and to work for the adoption of a binding UN resolution ensuring its effective implementation.

a5892.speaker: International Court of Justice (advisory opinion, as reported in the Tunisian statement)
a5892.name: International Court of Justice (advisory opinion
a5892.title: as reported in the Tunisian statement)
a5892.speech: Requires the occupying entity to allow the presence and activities of the UN, international organisations and third states in the occupied Palestinian territories; notably to guarantee the delivery of humanitarian aid and to provide health services in Gaza and across the Palestinian territories; to facilitate international relief operations, in particular those of UNRWA; to prohibit forced displacement and expulsions; and to prevent the use of starvation as a weapon of war.

a5934.speaker: Padenga Holdings (company statement)
a5934.name: Padenga Holdings (company statement)
a5934.speech: Says it will save approximately US$750,000 per year in energy costs from the installation of a solar power facility at its Pickstone Peerless Mine.

a5944.speaker: Human rights and health experts
a5944.name: Human rights and health experts
a5944.speech: Agree that this collaboration is extremely important, despite its potential impact and challenges.

a5944.speaker: Dr. Tunde Akanbi, expert
a5944.name: Dr. Tunde Akanbi
a5944.title: expert
a5944.speech: Stated that both the NHRC and NACA may face capacity constraints in terms of personnel, resources, and expertise required to effectively implement the collaboration, while the success of the initiative is heavily dependent on political will and commitment from both agencies and the government as a whole ; added that deep-rooted cultural and social norms that perpetuate stigma and discrimination may impede progress, necessitating ongoing community engagement and education ; suggests that effective collaboration necessitates strong coordination between the two agencies, which may be difficult to achieve in practice.

a5944.speaker: Dr Tony Ojukwu, Executive Secretary of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)
a5944.name: Dr Tony Ojukwu
a5944.title: Executive Secretary of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)
a5944.speech: Spoke at the inauguration in Abuja on Monday and expressed his displeasure with sexual preference-based criminalisation: “Access to justice is a critical component of human rights and the rule of law. It ensures that people, regardless of their socioeconomic status, gender, health condition, or background, can seek and obtain redress if their rights are violated. This forum is an important step towards strengthening our collective efforts to close the justice gap for people living with HIV/AIDS, key populations, and other marginalised groups who continue to face stigma, discrimination, and systemic barriers to legal redress and social justice.” ; lamented that “Despite significant progress in addressing HIV-related discrimination, many affected individuals continue to face violations of their rights in healthcare, employment, and social settings” ; “The passage of the Same-Sex Marriage Prohibition Act of 2014 has also brought to the forefront issues of discrimination, indiscriminate arrest, torture, and inhumane and degrading treatment of key populations in Nigeria. The NHRC and other organisations have been at the forefront of seeking justice for victims of human rights violations related to sexual or gender identity in Nigeria. We will not stop.” ; “With the support of the Global Fund, the NHRC will launch a series of programmes, capacity building, policy, and legal reforms to protect Nigerians' rights from discrimination and criminalisation over the next two years. We will also establish institutional measures to ensure access to justice and collaborate with other partners to support class and individual legal actions by Sections 5 and 6 of the NHRC (Amendment) Act of 2010.” ; stated that the NHRC is committed to collaborating closely with all stakeholders to protect human rights and promote social justice for all people, adding that no single agency, no matter how well-resourced, can achieve access to justice on its own.

a5944.speaker: Dr. Leopold Zekeng, Country Director of UNAIDS (represented by Oluwafisayo Fakayode)
a5944.name: Dr. Leopold Zekeng
a5944.title: Country Director of UNAIDS (represented by Oluwafisayo Fakayode)
a5944.speech: Stated that “people living with HIV/AIDS frequently face significant barriers to justice” – stigma, discrimination, a lack of awareness of their rights, insufficient legal support, institutional bias, and financial constraints – and that “This is a serious human rights issue that requires our immediate attention and action.” ; “At UNAIDS, we believe that justice is more than a concept; it is a fundamental human right that should be available to everyone, regardless of their health status, identity, or circumstances. The right to access justice is indeed multidimensional. It includes justiciability, availability, accessibility, high quality, the provision of remedies for victims and survivors, and the accountability of justice systems.” ; “This Access to Justice Coordination Forum demonstrates our unwavering commitment to removing the barriers that prevent individuals from receiving the justice they deserve. Addressing this issue requires a collaborative effort. Governments, civil society organisations, healthcare providers, legal practitioners, and communities must collaborate to foster an environment in which people living with HIV/AIDS can seek justice without fear or prejudice. To ensure that justice is accessible to all, we must share best practices, support one another's efforts, and hold each other accountable.”

a5944.speaker: Dr Temitope Ilori, Director General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a5944.name: Dr Temitope Ilori
a5944.title: Director General of the National Agency for the Control of AIDS (NACA)
a5944.speech: “NACA will continue to lead the national response to HIV/AIDS, and this collaboration with the NHRC will further empower the agency to address both the health and human rights dimensions of the epidemic.” ; “It is important to note that the success of this forum will be determined by our ability to collaborate across sectors, leveraging our diverse expertise to develop effective strategies that promote equitable access to justice for all Nigerians. We hope that this forum will help us all work together to create a more just and inclusive society. May this initiative be a model for future collaborations between Africa's health and justice sectors.”

a5944.speaker: Winnie Byanyima, UNAIDS Executive Director
a5944.name: Winnie Byanyima
a5944.title: UNAIDS Executive Director
a5944.speech: Stated, while meeting with Catholic Church leaders as part of a global effort to mobilise voices of faith: “Two weeks ago, the world's largest AIDS relief programme was paused. The United States government provides medication to 20 million HIV-positive people to keep them alive and prevent HIV infection. A humanitarian waiver was granted, allowing some lifesaving medications to be distributed. That is appreciated. However, the programme's future remains uncertain.” ; “HIV clinics around the world have closed, and HIV prevention and treatment programs have been halted. Without US funding, 6.3 million people will die within four years, while 8.9 million will contract HIV for the first time. Approximately 370,000 babies will contract HIV, and without treatment, half will not live to their second birthday.” ; “The AIDS movement has gone through this before. When people died as a result of neglect in the early days of HIV in Africa, Asia, and Latin America, it was the churches that stepped in to care for the sick and dying.” ; “The church has a powerful voice that reaches communities all over the world. In today's world, we need the voice and leadership of faith to defend the global AIDS response and life-saving programs like PEPFAR. Human life is sacred, and it is currently at risk.”

a5944.speaker: Catholic leaders
a5944.name: Catholic leaders
a5944.speech: Have urged the restoration of HIV programmes and other critical international funding.

a6127.speaker: Inge Zaamwani, Minister of Agriculture, Water, Fisheries and Land Reform (Namibia)
a6127.name: Inge Zaamwani
a6127.title: Minister of Agriculture, Water, Fisheries and Land Reform (Namibia)
a6127.speech: Questioned the industry's N$300 million contribution to government coffers, while the sector's revenue in 2024 was N$14 billion; revealed that the government collected N$278 million in 2024 through various streams, including fishing quota fees and by-catch penalties: “If you look at the total turnover of the industry in 2024 of N$14 billion and the owner of the resource is getting less than N$300 million, this is a point of reflection for us. We must reflect on it, and we must see how we can increase the value that is added to the resource and the value paid over to the owner of the resource, which is, of course, the government of Namibia on behalf of the people.”

a6127.speaker: Inge Zaamwani, Minister of Agriculture, Water, Fisheries and Land Reform (Namibia)
a6127.name: Inge Zaamwani
a6127.title: Minister of Agriculture, Water, Fisheries and Land Reform (Namibia)
a6127.speech: Said the industry remains a vital pillar of the economy even if its contribution to the GDP declined from 4.5 percent in 2023 to 4.1 percent in 2024, attributing the decline to continued decreases in the Total Allowable Catch in commercial species; “Notwithstanding the reduction in the TAC, the sector maintains robust operations with a fleet of 235 vessels and 30 onshore processing facilities. And those facilities produce a total of 39 value-added fish and fish products, reinforcing the sector's commitment to employment creation, value addition and economic growth”; stressed that the reduced TAC further affected the export earnings in 2024, which declined from N$14.1 billion a year before to N$13.8 billion.

a6127.speaker: Inge Zaamwani, Minister of Agriculture, Water, Fisheries and Land Reform (Namibia)
a6127.name: Inge Zaamwani
a6127.title: Minister of Agriculture, Water, Fisheries and Land Reform (Namibia)
a6127.speech: Said over 19,000 Namibians, the majority being female, were employed onshore by the industry, and emphasised the need to retain those jobs; is confident that consultations with the industry and technical experts would ensure an improved TAC next year to retain jobs.

a6188.speaker: Top UN official in Somalia (James Swan, UN Secretary General's Special Representative for Somalia)
a6188.name: Top UN official in Somalia (James Swan
a6188.title: UN Secretary General's Special Representative for Somalia)
a6188.speech: Told the UN Security Council on Thursday that the Somali government is looking ahead to its first direct elections in a half-century, in a time of dramatic crisis as a result of COVID-19 and floods that wreak havoc in parts of the country.

a6188.speaker: Office of Prime Minister Hassan Ali Khaire (statement)
a6188.name: Office of Prime Minister Hassan Ali Khaire (statement)
a6188.speech: Said the purpose of the national electoral law, which was endorsed by the Federal Parliament in December 2019, was to conduct free and fair elections, to identify the powers and responsibilities of the National Independent Electoral Commission (NIEC) and to define and describe the country's electoral system.

a6188.speaker: Hassan Ali Khaire, Prime Minister of Somalia
a6188.name: Hassan Ali Khaire
a6188.title: Prime Minister of Somalia
a6188.speech: "In the light of the constitutional review process, the Federal government and federal member states have reached a political agreement on the model of elections in the country and sharing natural resources," told the opening of the fifth session of the Upper House of the Federal parliament of Somalia on April 1, 2019 ; reiterated that the National Electoral Security Task Force, whose establishment he directed, will be a significant part of the efforts to guarantee the necessary security arrangements made ready for the country's voting to take place, including consensus building among political leaders and civil society so that the elections enjoy broad support and acceptance.

a6188.speaker: James Swan, United Nations Secretary General's Special Representative for Somalia
a6188.name: James Swan
a6188.title: United Nations Secretary General's Special Representative for Somalia
a6188.speech: Emphasized that holding peaceful, inclusive, credible and transparent one-person-one-vote elections would be a historic step in rebuilding Somalia and would assist with the country's continued democratic development ; "In addition to the focus on elections, we also note the importance of Somalia making progress on other critical state-building priorities. These include formation of the Constitutional Court, the Judicial Services Commission, and an independent Human Rights Commission, as well as completing the review of the Federal Constitution," said during a briefing to the UN Security Council on Thursday May 21.

a6193.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a6193.name: Donald Trump
a6193.title: US President
a6193.speech: Told the press on Sunday that the US Agency for International Development (USAID) "is run by radical lunatics" and that the White House is "trying to get them out" ; "Then we'll make a decision," he added, referring to the agency's future.

a6193.speaker: Two sources (a current and a former US official, anonymous) speaking to the Associated Press
a6193.name: Two sources (a current and a former US official
a6193.title: anonymous) speaking to the Associated Press
a6193.speech: Said the US administration removed two USAID security chiefs after they refused to hand over classified material to the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), headed by Elon Musk; and that the two were placed on leave. The sources spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorised to share the information.

a6193.speaker: Associated Press (AP)
a6193.name: Associated Press (AP)
a6193.speech: Identifies the sources as a current and a former US official, and reports that DOGE members finally obtained access on Saturday to USAID classified information, including intelligence reports, which had previously been denied to them.

a6193.speaker: Washington Post
a6193.name: Washington Post
a6193.speech: Indicated in Friday's edition that the acting deputy secretary of the Treasury, David Lebryk, is said to have resigned after more than 30 years of service after DOGE requested access to confidential department data.

a6486.speaker: Jerry Silaa, Minister for Communications and Information Technology (Tanzania)
a6486.name: Jerry Silaa
a6486.title: Minister for Communications and Information Technology (Tanzania)
a6486.speech: Made clear that if a citizen is unable to access a particular network, they should know that the Government has acted to protect the Tanzanian: “If you have noticed that on some network — it need not be X, any at all, even YouTube — there is something you are looking for and you do not get it, know that it is work being done by the Government to ensure it protects the consumer and to ensure that all those running services in our nation’s space comply with the law” ; said, in an interview with the Wasafi television station, that Section 16 of the Online Content Regulations of 2000 sets out the type of content that may be published on a given network, that those regulations are aimed at protecting the Tanzanian user and that where this is contravened the Government acts to protect the user: “After X was bought and then in May 2024 that network changed its privacy policy in a way that goes against that Tanzanian regulation. If you go on X you can come across pornographic images, things that go against our laws, culture, customs and traditions.”

a6486.speaker: Trader and influencer on X (anonymous, declined to be named)
a6486.name: Trader and influencer on X (anonymous
a6486.title: declined to be named)
a6486.speech: Complained about the difficulty of doing business because the number of customers able to reach X has fallen: “You know, those who get X now are those who use VPNs; many do not know about this, so that interaction has dropped considerably, and this makes many people unable to get information when there are new products” ; “Because they are not reaching the number of people they had aimed to reach, all this is money lost; for example, these companies I had were paying up to Sh1 million a month — you can see how much money we have lost.”

a6486.speaker: Another trader on X (anonymous)
a6486.name: Another trader on X (anonymous)
a6486.speech: Said the level of customers has dropped because those remaining on the network are the same ones, and even if they are the customers they will not buy every day: “You know, when people are many the scope of business becomes wider; when people are few even the turnover is small. Instead of shutting down the network there was a way to block the content they are complaining about — the authorities do exist” ; said rushing to shut down the entire network cannot solve the problem and instead leaves many young people who earned money through it without any source of income: “You know, here there are people who bring in a great deal of money working with various companies as influencers. I may not bring in much money, but there are those who bring in a lot; yet today companies have suspended contracts, and their income is falling.”

a6486.speaker: Another influencer (anonymous)
a6486.name: Another influencer (anonymous)
a6486.speech: Said the matter caused him to lose a contract that would have brought him Sh9 million, money he says would have helped him meet his needs and make progress in life: “You may think it is a joke, but it is the reality. When we were at the final stages of completing this deal I saw that X had been blocked; put yourself in my shoes, half of the money was to be paid to me when I began the work and the remaining percentage would have been paid to me bit by bit until the period ended. I had already done my calculations, and the result is that I ended up seeing that money only on paper” ; called on the Government to step up its efforts to control the content it does not want to reach the public rather than shutting down the whole network and affecting other young people earning a living there.

a6486.speaker: Legal and Human Rights Centre (LHRC) (public statement)
a6486.name: Legal and Human Rights Centre (LHRC) (public statement)
a6486.speech: Condemned the Government’s decision to block access to the social network X and called on the Government to restore X along with access to Clubhouse, Telegram and other blocked digital platforms: “Also, the Government should ensure there is transparency in the process of digital regulation and involve stakeholders in preparing content-management policies that uphold human rights” ; called on citizens, civil society organisations and the international community to stand together as one force to defend and protect digital freedom in Tanzania.

a6641.speaker: Joint FAO-WFP report (Early Warning Analysis of Acute Food Insecurity Hotspots), by the Food and Agriculture Organization and the World Food Programme
a6641.name: Joint FAO-WFP report (Early Warning Analysis of Acute Food Insecurity Hotspots)
a6641.title: by the Food and Agriculture Organization and the World Food Programme
a6641.speech: Raised the alarm on 20 countries including Ethiopia, saying that acute food insecurity levels appear to be reaching new highs globally as a result of the socio-economic fallout of measures imposed to contain the spread of COVID-19 ; warned that hotspots in four countries - Burkina Faso, Yemen, South Sudan and Nigeria - are on the brink of severe levels of food insecurity and could potentially fall into famine within three to six months as the coronavirus pandemic erodes people's ability to access food ; found that millions of people who were already facing hunger are on the brink of famine as the pandemic plunders employment, disrupts agricultural activities, slashes remittances and sends crude prices spiralling ; said 20 countries and situations are likely to face potential spikes in high acute food insecurity in the next three to six months and require urgent attention.

a6641.speaker: Margot van der Velden, WFP director of emergencies
a6641.name: Margot van der Velden
a6641.title: WFP director of emergencies
a6641.speech: "We are at a catastrophic turning point. Once again, we face the risk of famine in four different parts of the world at the same time."

a6641.speaker: 2020 Global Report on Food Crises - September 2020 update
a6641.name: 2020 Global Report on Food Crises - September 2020 update
a6641.speech: According to the report, the COVID-19 pandemic has exacerbated these pre-existing and on-going drivers, mainly by causing economic activities to decline, which in turn led to income loss and reduced household purchasing power, and a multitude of food-system wide shocks.

a6676.speaker: Catherine Uri-Khos, founder of Okahandja Home-based Caregivers
a6676.name: Catherine Uri-Khos
a6676.title: founder of Okahandja Home-based Caregivers
a6676.speech: Said they were given the building by the municipality in 2004; according to her, the agreement between them and the municipality was that after 10 years of operation, the founders can take over the premises, provided they renovate it themselves: "Ten years lapsed and they still refuse to hand over the building to us. If they say this is their building, then they should compensate us N$500 000 in damages for costs incurred or else they must give us the building as per the agreement taken in 2004. We are not going to vacate until this issue is solved in good faith. They must compensate us before we vacate."

a6676.speaker: Natasha Brinkman, Okahandja mayor
a6676.name: Natasha Brinkman
a6676.title: Okahandja mayor
a6676.speech: Confirmed the eviction notices given to the duo to vacate municipal premises and that both have defied the order; said the building belongs to the municipality and she doesn't understand why the founders of the project are fighting for it: "Why should they use money from tenants for their use under the pretext of home-based care? She even called me threatening me that she will beat me up. We won't compensate them. They don't even have proof or any receipt, which shows how much they spent to renovate the building. I have a council resolution that they must hand over the building to the rightful owner. The rightful owner is the municipality" ; the mayor promised that the duo and the council would have a meeting to discuss and find a solution to this issue soon.

a6676.speaker: Magdalena Meyer, founder of Okahandja Home-based Caregivers
a6676.name: Magdalena Meyer
a6676.title: founder of Okahandja Home-based Caregivers
a6676.speech: Said the municipality at the time told them to take the building as it is and their condition was to renovate it themselves; explained that since the building was dilapidated, with the financial assistance from USAID and Namdeb they got funds and renovated the building, and that they also brought water and electricity to the premises.

a6679.speaker: Government of Mozambique
a6679.name: Government of Mozambique
a6679.speech: Says problems on the ground forced a readjustment of the delivery deadlines to February 2025; had gone on to point to the month of December as the deadline after the works were not completed in August.

a6679.speaker: Jeronimo Mutisse, spokesperson for the provincial infrastructure service
a6679.name: Jeronimo Mutisse
a6679.title: spokesperson for the provincial infrastructure service
a6679.speech: "Over this period production has been above 270 thousand tonnes. However, the volume of exports has been lower, yielding annual revenue of 17 million meticais for the state coffers" ; "Recently, the officials of Dingsheng announced to us that around 270 thousand tonnes of zircon and ilmenite, produced at the Chibuto Heavy Sands, are awaiting export. Without specifying the period during which the production has been stored, they cite difficulties faced because of the high costs of road transport to the Port of Maputo."

a6679.speaker: Officials of Dingsheng
a6679.name: Officials of Dingsheng
a6679.speech: Announced that around 270 thousand tonnes of zircon and ilmenite produced at the Chibuto Heavy Sands are awaiting export, citing difficulties faced because of the high costs of road transport to the Port of Maputo.

a6679.speaker: Artur Macamo, administrator of the Chongoene district
a6679.name: Artur Macamo
a6679.title: administrator of the Chongoene district
a6679.speech: Explains that the delay is due to problems on the ground, which forced a readjustment of the deadlines "to February 2025."

a6691.speaker: Robert Bourgi, former influential player in France-Africa relations
a6691.name: Robert Bourgi
a6691.title: former influential player in France-Africa relations
a6691.speech: Declared that France was showing itself to be ungrateful, citing the cases of Presidents Mobutu and Bongo, to whom Paris refused humanitarian visas at the end of their lives despite the services they had rendered to France ; in his book "They know that I know everything. My life in France-Africa" he sets out in great detail these behaviours which he judges unworthy ; on a television set he recounted how Marshal Mobutu, the former president of what is today the DRC, had been abandoned by France after his fall, and that President Jacques Chirac, Elysee Secretary-General Dominique de Villepin and Prime Minister Alain Juppe remained deaf to his request for treatment in France ; "Omar Bongo died in a clinic in Barcelona, when he had previously been treated by leading professors at the American Hospital in Neuilly. In the end, he was no longer received, he was no longer considered. France is ungrateful."

a6691.speaker: Emmanuel Macron, President of France
a6691.name: Emmanuel Macron
a6691.title: President of France
a6691.speech: During his last meeting with French diplomats had described Africans as "ungrateful" for having driven the colonial army out of their territories.

a6691.speaker: Mobutu Sese Seko, former President of Zaire/DRC (reported by Robert Bourgi)
a6691.name: Mobutu Sese Seko
a6691.title: former President of Zaire/DRC (reported by Robert Bourgi)
a6691.speech: Gravely ill, he had expressed to Bourgi his wish to come to France for treatment.

a6704.speaker: Alexander Kofi-Mensah Mould, Chief Executive of the Millennium Development Authority (MiDA)
a6704.name: Alexander Kofi-Mensah Mould
a6704.title: Chief Executive of the Millennium Development Authority (MiDA)
a6704.speech: "Through the MCC Compact, we developed proven, high-impact models ready for nationwide implementation." ; "We're now building on that foundation to support food security, economic diversification, and rural industrialization under Grow24." ; said MiDA's broad experience in infrastructure, energy, and agro-industrial development makes it ideally suited to drive large-scale agricultural initiatives across the country ; explained that core components from the Compact - such as land preparation, irrigation engineering, and integrated agronomic systems - will be adapted and scaled to meet Grow24's ambitious targets; described ongoing efforts to clear and level land using precision methods, alongside the design of advanced irrigation systems tailored to various landscapes ; said MiDA's role will be to provide the technical and managerial backbone necessary for the long-term success of the initiative ; "Grow24 represents a bold new vision for agricultural development in Ghana, and MiDA is fully prepared to deliver on that promise."

a6771.speaker: Sources close to the matter (anonymous)
a6771.name: Sources close to the matter (anonymous)
a6771.speech: According to sources close to the matter, the United States under the presidency of Donald Trump appears to be intensifying its "withdrawal" from the African continent with the decision to put an end to the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC), after the suspension of USAID earlier in the year; partner countries are expected to be officially notified within 40 days, and only Senegal and Cote d'Ivoire will be granted additional time to complete their ongoing projects, notably in the energy and urban transport sectors.

a7022.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State (social media post)
a7022.name: Marco Rubio
a7022.title: US Secretary of State (social media post)
a7022.speech: Commented on social media that Rasool “was no longer welcome in our great country”.

a7022.speaker: Ebrahim Rasool, South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.name: Ebrahim Rasool
a7022.title: South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.speech: “I want to start with an issue of perspective because how South Africa responds to this current relationship with the USA is going to demand quite a lot of perspective from us... foreign policy, like other policies, is like a telescope. It has two lenses. A lens of your values and a lens of your interests... I think South Africa has by and large held the lens of values to its eye and then viewed its interest and calibrated its interest through that lens. I think that there are definitely countries who invert the telescope and put their interest against their eyes and then calibrate their values.”

a7022.speaker: Ebrahim Rasool, South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.name: Ebrahim Rasool
a7022.title: South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.speech: Said it is useful to recognise the many continuities in the Trump administration inherited from the Biden administration: “it was Biden that started putting pressure... on AGOA for South Africa as a result of some of our geopolitical stances”; “It's a continuity from the Biden administration where the resistance to the emerging multipolarity in the world started to be articulated, and it is from the Biden administration that we saw the very frenetic attempts to maintain US ideological hegemony, particularly in the way in which it armed, for example, Ukraine and Israel, for that hegemony”; “we must not miss the continuities from the Biden administration.”

a7022.speaker: Ebrahim Rasool, South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.name: Ebrahim Rasool
a7022.title: South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.speech: On the discontinuities of the Trump administration: “there is a disrespect for the institutional base of the current hegemonic order”, seen in the Russian negotiations, attitudes to NATO and the UN, and “the bypassing of monies from the US from the World Bank, IMF”; “what Donald Trump is launching, is an assault on incumbency - those who are in power, by mobilising a supremacism against the incumbency at home”, linked to “very clear data that shows great demographic shifts in the USA in which the voting electorate in the USA is projected to become 48% white, and that the possibility of a majority of minorities is looming on the horizon”; “there is also an export of the revolution. It's no accident that Elon Musk has involved himself in UK politics and elevated a Nigel Farage and reform movement”, as with Vice President Vance addressing the Alternative für Deutschland; and the role of Afrikaners is “to project white victimhood as a dog whistle that there is a global protective movement that is beginning to envelop embattled white communities”; “It's a transition from soft impunity to hard impunity, in-your-face impunity. It's a transition from rules-based duress to punitive coercion, naked punitive coercion, as the currency of exchange.”

a7022.speaker: Ebrahim Rasool, South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.name: Ebrahim Rasool
a7022.title: South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.speech: On the power being exercised: “I think the power exercised is of the shock and awe variety”; “the shock and awe is being exercised across the USA, we've seen DOGE (Department of Government Efficiency) at work, we've seen the borders, we've seen the attack on DEI (diversity, equity and inclusion) and wokeism, and we've seen social cuts in the USA. Second, at a global level we all know that the stopping of aid and assistance, the multilateral financing system is brought down through, for example, anything that sounds like climate, like the JETP (Just Energy Transition Programme). The trade and tariffs is dominating the agenda and the geopolitical”; “South Africa fits into that... because we are the historical antidote to supremacism, the success story of it”, and “our GNU is seen as the second miracle of the democratic era in South Africa.”

a7022.speaker: Ebrahim Rasool, South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.name: Ebrahim Rasool
a7022.title: South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.speech: On South Africa's strategic dilemmas: “we have what is called the hot-button issues: Israel and the ICJ, the Afrikaner issues, BRICS and the de-dollarisation, China and Taiwan and the liaison office, the allegation of Iran funding, and the Russia/Ukraine thing - is receding on that. And then there's the bread-and-butter economics, like the aid budgets that slashed $8 billion from South Africa, at the very least, the tariffs and trade that I think we're being threatened with, AGOA comes into that very quickly.”

a7022.speaker: Ebrahim Rasool, South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.name: Ebrahim Rasool
a7022.title: South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.speech: Set out six interventions for South Africa: “The first thing is stay calm and don't panic... I think we've got to let the push-back and the walk-back mature in the USA and see what the town hall meetings are doing to next year's electoral projections”; “the Afrikaner issue creates outrage in South Africa, but it has created enormous self-mobilisation behind South Africa. It consolidates our African base, it returns old allies... don't panic in South Africa about it. It's working in our favour in the USA”; “we're engaging the lawmakers and we're putting in deposits so that when fear subsides of the White House, we have planted the alternative view”; “let other formations that are coming here have their say. Let's absorb it... respond comprehensively, not toe-to-toe”; “let's hold our impact players back, like our envoys and so forth. Because you don't come to empty doors. The administration is not yet filled. In (the) State Department there is no Africa division in place... You're knocking on empty doors”; “don't come empty-handed. Be ready to deal... You saw the Zelensky effect. If you prevaricate, you're a loser”; and “manage the G20 handover - salvage that baby from the bath water.”

a7022.speaker: Ebrahim Rasool, South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.name: Ebrahim Rasool
a7022.title: South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.speech: On the embassy's sensemaking work: “we have in the last four weeks surveyed all shades of opinion on the Hill, through targeting over 20 offices and representatives and senators”; “Every day my staff works out whatever the implications are of every executive order and they're over a hundred already”; “Is our strategy to wait and watch? I don't think we're waiting but we are watching”; and warned that to join “the kind of appellation of President Trump as a buffoon... you make the cardinal mistake of underestimating at least the impact of what is being done.”

a7022.speaker: Ebrahim Rasool, South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.name: Ebrahim Rasool
a7022.title: South African Ambassador to the United States
