a7022.speech: On trade, AGOA and de-dollarisation: “we can't afford to make a simple binary of our options”; “there's no escaping from one regime of trade to another” in moving from AGOA to the GSP; “De-dollarisation - Not even China is speaking any longer about de-dollarisation, Russia certainly isn't speaking about de-dollarisation, because not only is that a performative issue at this moment, it's not practical. It does not economically make sense for us to even breathe that”; “We want it [AGOA] to be renewed. But we need contingencies”; “there is a difference in our exports to China and our exports to the USA. Our exports to China are 80% commodity-based. Our exports to the US are 70% manufactured. The one comes with an enormous number of jobs.”

a7022.speaker: Ebrahim Rasool, South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.name: Ebrahim Rasool
a7022.title: South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.speech: On values versus interests and allies: “we must not see values and interests as binary issues. Because to sustain a human rights culture in South Africa may look like a very values-based thing, but it needs you to put food on the table in every household”; “we must avoid all or nothing kind of things (like) if the EU can't agree with us on this and keep their funds flowing, then they are not an ally. Sometimes, there are strength in numbers, that there are common victimhood that must be turned into agency”; and said one of his non-negotiables in Washington is South Africa's bottom line on the ICJ.

a7022.speaker: Ebrahim Rasool, South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.name: Ebrahim Rasool
a7022.title: South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.speech: On South Africa building self-reliance in HIV funding: “almost two decades ago our input into HIV funding was near zero, and PEPFAR was near 100%. In 2025, PEPFAR is 17% and the South African government is 83%. That's a success story, and that's a story that says the bridge is almost reaching the other side.”

a7022.speaker: Ebrahim Rasool, South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.name: Ebrahim Rasool
a7022.title: South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.speech: On the “Zelensky effect” and negotiating with the White House: “the kind of public display that we saw in the White House is not what you subject your people to with unprepared ways to go into a transactional negotiation with the White House... We've got our top lines. We've got our bottom lines. Let's open the discussion”; “it is not about selling off and giving away critical minerals, it's how we understand our leverages within this.”

a7022.speaker: Ebrahim Rasool, South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.name: Ebrahim Rasool
a7022.title: South African Ambassador to the United States
a7022.speech: On criticism of his own approach, the media and the President: “I've not thought that what I've said sounded like left-wing militancy... I fear more that people that I've been associated with historically, may [have] thought that I'm too soft in being pragmatic”; “when you get access, you shut up, because you've got to nurture it. You don't conduct the kind of fate of 60 million people on television, on video, on social media”; “the way in which the Presidency, DIRCO, DTIC, agriculture and others have conducted themselves have been with absolute dignity”; “we cannot feed the performative beast. Too much is at stake”; “We're not going to compete with a Kallie [Kriel] and Ernst [Roets]... They were found to have feet of clay”; “we've got to show firm feet, up for the game, confident about our bottom lines, and open to negotiate our top lines... Values will always be there, but transnationality, I've learned, is not going to be a swear word unless it's a cover for larceny. And we will not open South Africa to larceny.”

a7022.speaker: Cyril Ramaphosa, South African President (as reported by Rasool)
a7022.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
a7022.title: South African President (as reported by Rasool)
a7022.speech: “Our president can stand up in the State of the Nation Address and say we will not be bullied”; under pressure to “send your envoys, send your envoys”, the president says he will do it at the strategic time.

a7022.speaker: “South Africa's National Interest” framework document
a7022.name: “South Africa's National Interest” framework document
a7022.speech: Says that South Africa's national interests “are those interests that are based on strategic ones where our goals and objectives that are needed for our nation's economy and security well-being that it would consist by and large of matters for example of defence that protect our nation, matters of economy that ensure the well-being of our nation, matters of the world order interests in which we need a global system that facilitates our mutual protection and well-being with other countries and that we also have ideological interest to advance the values for universal good”.

a7022.speaker: Joel Pollak, author of the book The Agenda (South African in MAGA inner circles)
a7022.name: Joel Pollak
a7022.title: author of the book The Agenda (South African in MAGA inner circles)
a7022.speech: Speaks about the 200 executive orders that must be prosecuted within the first 100 days.

a7022.speaker: Wandile Sihlobo, fellow webinar panellist
a7022.name: Wandile Sihlobo
a7022.title: fellow webinar panellist
a7022.speech: As Wandile (Sihlobo) has said, this is not a moment to antagonise the United States.

a7290.speaker: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda, Minister of Health of Malawi
a7290.name: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda
a7290.title: Minister of Health of Malawi
a7290.speech: Has disclosed that 14,000 youths contract HIV every year in Malawi, saying the figures have dropped compared to 2016 in which 22,000 youths contracted the virus ; “Research findings show that 14,000 young people in Malawi contract HIV every year. This clearly shows that young people indulge in unprotected sex.”

a7290.speaker: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda, Minister of Health of Malawi
a7290.name: Khumbize Kandodo Chiponda
a7290.title: Minister of Health of Malawi
a7290.speech: Said the government intends to end the Aids pandemic by 2030 and called on young people to refrain from risky behaviours that can facilitate the transmission of HIV ; Chiponda also called on faith leaders, traditional leaders and all Malawians to put in place necessary measures that can help to protect young men from contracting HIV.

a7290.speaker: Dr Chipo Kanjo, National Aids Commission (NAC) Board Chairperson
a7290.name: Dr Chipo Kanjo
a7290.title: National Aids Commission (NAC) Board Chairperson
a7290.speech: Called on Malawians to respect the rights of people living with HIV as Malawi strives to end the Aids pandemic by 2030. The NAC Board Chairperson said that disclosing a person's HIV status without consent is a total violation of rights.

a7290.speaker: Amy Diaz, Chief of Mission at the American Embassy in Malawi
a7290.name: Amy Diaz
a7290.title: Chief of Mission at the American Embassy in Malawi
a7290.speech: Said in the last five years, the American Government provided 2 billion US dollars to Malawi for HIV and Aids response.

a7420.speaker: Bank of Mozambique (statistical report)
a7420.name: Bank of Mozambique (statistical report)
a7420.speech: According to data from the central bank, the cost of fuel imports by Mozambique fell 15% in 2024, to the equivalent of €1.085 billion, the lowest figure since the Covid-19 pandemic ; According to a statistical report from the Bank of Mozambique to which Lusa had access this Friday, the country’s fuel imports from January to December amounted to almost US$1.198 billion (€1.085 billion), while in the whole of 2023 the bill reached US$1.417 billion (€1.283 billion).

a7420.speaker: Ministry of Finance of Mozambique (budget execution report)
a7420.name: Ministry of Finance of Mozambique (budget execution report)
a7420.speech: “Gross domestic product at market prices (GDPpm) showed a negative variation of 4.87% in the fourth quarter of 2024, when compared to the same period in 2023, totalling 1.85% [for the year],” reads the budget execution report for last year from the Ministry of Finance ; the document also acknowledges “the negative impact of the post-election demonstrations recorded in the last quarter of 2024”, which “affected economic and social activities”.

a7420.speaker: Bank of Mozambique
a7420.name: Bank of Mozambique
a7420.speech: Announced measures to promote the availability of foreign currency to cover import needs ; announced in June, 2023, that it would no longer contribute to the country’s fuel import bills abroad, considering that the amounts can already be borne by commercial banks.

a7420.speaker: Silvina de Abreu, administrator of the central bank at the time
a7420.name: Silvina de Abreu
a7420.title: administrator of the central bank at the time
a7420.speech: Explained that the contribution dated back to 2005 and reached 100% after 2010, because there were “large amounts, ranging from US$10 to US$20 million in a single invoice”, making them unbearable for a bank or group of banks to support ; added that in recent years, “invoices have become quite fragmented”, sometimes in the order of “one million dollars or less”, which allows smaller banks to enter “this fuel financing market.”

a7489.speaker: Global Displacement Forecast Report 2025, released by the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a7489.name: Global Displacement Forecast Report 2025
a7489.title: released by the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
a7489.speech: Shows that ongoing conflict and attacks on civilians are fuelling increased displacement across West and Central Africa, including in Nigeria; identified Nigeria, Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger, Cameroon, Chad, and the Central African Republic as the most affected countries, warning that millions are at risk due to escalating displacement, disease outbreaks, and instability; Burkina Faso alone is expected to see over 200,000 additional displaced people by the end of 2026, with similar trends emerging in neighbouring countries.

a7489.speaker: Global Displacement Forecast Report 2025 (OCHA)
a7489.name: Global Displacement Forecast Report 2025 (OCHA)
a7489.speech: Highlighted multiple disease outbreaks in Nigeria’s northeast, particularly in Adamawa and Yobe States, where health authorities are battling cholera, measles, cerebrospinal meningitis (CSM), diphtheria, pertussis, and vaccine-derived poliovirus type 2 (VDPV2); indicated that Adamawa has recorded 41 cholera cases resulting in three deaths, along with 54 measles cases and one fatality, and 55 cases of CSM leading to 13 deaths; in Yobe, 445 suspected measles cases, 161 diphtheria cases, six VDPV2 cases, and 88 CSM cases have been reported, with eight deaths each from diphtheria and CSM; further stated that efforts to contain these outbreaks are severely constrained by inadequate funding, logistical challenges, low vaccination coverage, and limited laboratory capacity, raising concerns that the situation could escalate.

a7489.speaker: Global Displacement Forecast Report 2025 (OCHA)
a7489.name: Global Displacement Forecast Report 2025 (OCHA)
a7489.speech: Reported that escalating violence in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has forced the closure of Fataki General Hospital in Djugu Territory, leaving over 100,000 people without access to essential healthcare; on 14 March, local health authorities ordered the hospital’s closure due to worsening insecurity, medical staff and patients were relocated to safer areas, but overwhelmed health centres in these locations are struggling to meet demand, forcing many pregnant women to give birth at home without medical assistance; stated that between 29 January and 10 March, an estimated 15,000 displaced persons returned to Rutshuru Territory from Goma and Uganda, but with no humanitarian organisations currently operational in the area, returnees lack access to healthcare, mental health support, food, and other basic necessities despite the region’s relatively stable security.

a7513.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a7513.name: Donald Trump
a7513.title: US President
a7513.speech: Announced the conclusion of a ceasefire agreement in Gaza.

a7513.speaker: Moroccan Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Cooperation and Moroccans Residing Abroad (statement)
a7513.name: Moroccan Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a7513.title: African Cooperation and Moroccans Residing Abroad (statement)
a7513.speech: Said Morocco, whose king chairs the Al-Quds Committee, welcomed US President Donald Trump's announcement of the conclusion of a ceasefire agreement in Gaza, and expressed the Kingdom's "high appreciation" for the sustained initiatives and personal commitment of President Trump, stressing that these had "contributed decisively" to the conclusion of this hope-bearing agreement; also hailed the joint efforts of all the mediators involved in the search for a lasting truce in the Gaza Strip.

a7513.speaker: Moroccan Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Cooperation and Moroccans Residing Abroad (statement)
a7513.name: Moroccan Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a7513.title: African Cooperation and Moroccans Residing Abroad (statement)
a7513.speech: Called on "all parties to fully implement this agreement", in order to preserve human lives, allow the release of hostages and prisoners, and guarantee the rapid and sufficient delivery of humanitarian aid; insisted on the need to launch reconstruction operations without delay and to open the way to a "just, comprehensive and lasting" solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

a7513.speaker: Moroccan Ministry of Foreign Affairs, African Cooperation and Moroccans Residing Abroad (statement)
a7513.name: Moroccan Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a7513.title: African Cooperation and Moroccans Residing Abroad (statement)
a7513.speech: Reaffirming its position of principle, the Kingdom recalled its attachment to the two-state solution, the only viable basis for a just and lasting peace, resting on the creation of an independent and sovereign Palestinian state within the borders of 4 June 1967, with Al-Quds Acharif as its capital, including the Gaza Strip, living side by side with the State of Israel in security and peace; reiterated its "full readiness" to participate actively in all the stages and mechanisms put in place to guarantee the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people and contribute to the stability of the entire Middle East.
